Sports.title: Gianni Infantino comes out fighting: FIFA hit out at campaign to bring president down following bombshell allegation of his 'affair' with former UEFA staffer
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino comes out fighting: FIFA hit out at campaign to bring president down following bombshell allegation of his 'affair' with former UEFA staffer

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gianni Infantino has launched a two-footed assault on UEFA as he battles to save his FIFA presidency.

UEFA announced on Thursday that they will continue to boycott FIFA competitions if Infantino remains at the top of world football after his scandalous plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes to private investors collapsed.

Meanwhile, Infantino has also faced allegations this week that UEFA made a 'departure payment' to a female employee with whom he is alleged to have been in a relationship with while general secretary of European football’s governing body.

UEFA have confirmed a payment was made, but FIFA labelled the allegation as ‘categorically untrue’.

Another turbulent week in football governance culminated in FIFA slamming Infantino’s critics in a 315-word statement on Saturday evening - accusing both the media and UEFA of a smear campaign against the organisation's chief.

‘Echoing the recent statements of CONMEBOL and CAF, as well as discussions with FIFA Member Associations and Confederations from around the world, FIFA will not support, facilitate or tolerate any process concerning the election of the FIFA President that is inconsistent with FIFA’s Statutes, democratic procedures and established governance framework,’ the statement read.

‘The FIFA President was democratically elected by FIFA’s Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate.

‘It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President.

'Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously,' a statement released by football's governing body read earlier

‘Those who do not have the support of FIFA’s Member Associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA’s established democratic processes.

‘Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its President. Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

‘The FIFA President has dedicated more than 30 years of his professional life to European and world football, contributing to significant change in the game and, in particular, to broadening access, resources and opportunity across world football.

‘Change inevitably challenges established interests, but disagreement with that change cannot justify efforts to undermine the democratic mandate of FIFA’s President or the institution he was elected to lead.

‘FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously.

‘FIFA’s responsibility is to its 211 Member Associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our Member Associations and continuing the work of making football truly global.

‘Through the FIFA President and the FIFA administration, our focus remains firmly on that mission, and we are more determined than ever to fulfil it.’

UEFA have become increasingly isolated in their resistance to Infantino, with only CONCACAF - the body for North, Central America and the Caribbean - taking a similar stance to the European governing body. There have been fractures in that opposition, however, with Mexico rallying behind Infantino.

UEFA are the sole continental confederation boycotting FIFA tournaments, which one source described to Daily Mail Sport as ‘the only way to force Infantino out’. But, with the endorsement of Africa, Asia and South America, he can fight on.

As it stands, the FIFA president appears to have enough support to survive a vote of no confidence and secure a fourth term in next March’s election.

Sports.title: In the rabble of racecourses, The Jockey Club may well have fired the starting pistol on a commercial arms race
Sports.content:
In the rabble of racecourses, The Jockey Club may well have fired the starting pistol on a commercial arms race

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Racing politics does not quite garner the interest as the footballing equivalent.

While the sport is nowhere near the levels of the FIFA farce presided over by the ridiculous Gianni Infantino, the move by The Jockey Club to split from The Racecourse Association (RCA) is a significant move.

For years, racing has accepted that the status quo of governance will not help the sport’s interest in the long term. For years, nothing has been done about it.

Ascot announced its intention to quit RCA and The Jockey Club, which controls major racecourses such as Cheltenham, Aintree, Newmarket and Epsom, will follow suit by the end of the year.

There is one obvious fear here. The big guns fancy going it alone and the British Horseracing Authority (BHA) must be wise to it. Lord Charles Allen barely had his feet under the desk as BHA chief before he was undermined by the racecourses.

He wanted an element of commercial control and was quickly kicked aside. Allen quickly left his post and has been recently replaced by Simon Cox.

The Jockey Club look poised to primarily focus on festivals such as the Grand National

Kempton hosted a thrilling King George on Boxing Day but the future of the course is in doubt

CEO Jim Mullen has revealed that The Jockey Club will leave The Racecourse Association

There is now a general air of acceptance that any say in the financial interest of individual racecourses is beyond the BHA. That’s a concession they can afford to give away, however. The BHA ought to focus on their main objective in governing the sport.

Cox can say to the racecourses; OK, have full commercial control but give us more say in regulatory matters that might cross-over into the BHA brief. Things such as fixture list control might be a better hill to die on than commercial interests.

The concern for the BHA here is that independent racecourses get badly left behind. So much so that some fall by the wayside. Ascot has increased prize money for major races like the King George. This weekend’s Shergar Cup is a niche event but has good money.

The Jockey Club have struck the odd commercial deal and their interests suggest they are funnelling resources to the top end; more big races at Aintree, maximising Cheltenham and Newmarket while rejuvenating Epsom. All of this is happening as the future of Kempton, also in the Jockey Club portfolio, is in doubt.

Jockey Club chief executive Jim Mullen was the strongest initial ally to Lord Allen and, now he’s had long enough in the job, he knows exactly what he wants for The Jockey Club. The assessment phase is over and Mullen may well have spied an opportunity to seize a jump start on racing’s commercial assets.

The ball is now firmly in the court of RCA. Racecourses, large and small independents, will have to decide whether they want to stick or twist.

Arena Racing Company and their boss Martin Cruddace also have a major part to play in all this. The BHA, for the moment, can only look on and see how this racecourse rabble pans out.

Variety and accessibility are two enormous assets to British racing that might now be very much under threat.

Mullen may have just fired the starting pistol on a new commercial arms race and created a two-tier environment where the big races and festivals get bigger but the small every day meetings shrivel and die out.

ABSENCE OF RACING LEAGUE A MAJOR HELP TO THE SHERGAR CUP

For over 20 years the Shergar Cup is mainly seen as a harmless weekend of fun.

It’s a rare raceday where team sport comes to the fore. This is a bone of contention for punters as racing, while it’s a collective effort to get a horse ready to perform, is an individual sport.

It’s a hard betting medium at the best of times. Unfamiliar jockeys, different colours and perhaps a lower than overall standard expected in the saddle. The team aspect means little.

Team Great Britain and Ireland celebrate their success in the Shergar Cup

One isolated race meeting can be tolerated by the racing public and the Shergar Cup is now unique again thanks to the binning of the Racing League. It also gives people from different racing jurisdictions a chance to shine and get to know riders from across the world.

There’s not much of a material difference in that failed concept, except it ran at the same time in the calendar and lasted SIX weeks.

One day? Yes. One day that’s spread over six weeks? No thanks.

PERFORMANCE OF THE WEEK…

Time will tell about the strength of the form of the 21-length victory by FORTITUDINE in a Class Three Kempton novice on Wednesday night but the Godolphin-owned juvenile could hardly have created a strong visual impression.

He has been gelded and went off 7-2, which suggests this performance was something of a surprise to the Charlie Appleby yard, but he was quick away from a wide draw and effortlessly powered clear.

A brother to Rebel’s Romance, Fortitudine has the pedigree to make a splash at the top level but being a gelding will limit some of his loftier ambitions in his fledgling career.

SELECTIONS OF THE DAY…

Big Mojo drops in class in the Group Three Phoenix Sprint Stakes (Curragh, 3.25) but he’s been racing so keenly that he’s not given himself much chance of staying six furlongs.

The favourite is taken on with fellow British raider JAMES’S DELIGHT (5/2, Sky Bet). The Clive Cox-trained sprinter has smart course form and his latest effort has been strongly franked. He can track Big Mojo and Bucanero Fuerte into this and pick them off late.

SUN GODDESS (5/4 William Hill) can make it an 18th victory in the Group One Keeneland Phoenix Stakes (Curragh, 4.00). She was beaten in the Albany Stakes at Royal Ascot and scrambled home in a Group Two last time out. Stall two looks a good draw to sit handily and she might have too much class for the rest of the field before stepping up in trip later in the season.

France have won the last three renewals of the Prix Maurice de Gheest (Deauville, 3.40) and can make it four in a row with STOLEN KISS (7/2, bet365). He ran a blinder when fourth at Royal Ascot in the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes and can repel the challenge of 1,000 Guineas winner True Love to win this Group One contest for Marseille-based trainer Patrice Cottier.

Sports.title: Inside Matthias Jaissle's first 72 hours as Newcastle boss: A magician, a new training ground mantra and the banned topic of discussion among Toon bosses - plus insiders reveal how 38-year-old dazzled in job interview
Sports.content:
In a restaurant in Murcia on Friday night, Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle was struck by two things about the magician entertaining him and his squad.

Firstly, the magic, and a sleight of hand that saw members of his party relieved of expensive watches, much to the amusement of those around them.

But secondly, and perhaps more so, the fact the club had thought to fly in the conjurer from the North East specifically for this introductory, team-bonding evening. The new boss, it is said, paused to appreciate the attention to detail.

Because if Newcastle are to survive this season - note, their relegation odds have been cut to single figures this week - Jaissle will need that same meticulous application in every aspect of his own operation. There is no illusion here, a Premier League rookie has inherited a situation that more experienced managers would have sidestepped.

For once the tapas dishes were cleared and watches returned to their rightful owners, the German would have realised there is no time to waste. A 2-1 friendly win over 10-man Valencia here in Spain may have marked his first game in charge on Saturday night, but in just two weeks’ time Liverpool await at St James’ Park in the Premier League.

Premier League rookie Matthias Jaissle has taken on a sizeable task at Newcastle

The new Toon boss appreciated the attention to detail when the club flew a North East magician to perform tricks at a team-bonding evening in Spain

Already, inside his first 72 hours, Jaissle has lost the club’s captain, Bruno Guimaraes, to Arsenal. Before that, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali were sold to balance spending-rules deficits. The five players brought in have never played in the Premier League and four of them are aged 20 or under. There was a concern over goals last season and two of the top scorers, Gordon and Guimaraes, have now gone.

From afar, and even up close, a campaign of struggle appears more likely than not. The fact Eddie Howe stood down after originally deciding to carry on is informative. Not that those who remain on the inside share the view that a traumatic summer will extend into autumn and beyond.

Rather, beneath a Spanish sun this week, there has been optimism. There is now a steadfast belief that a reset was needed, on both the balance sheet and football pitch. Howe himself suspected that a fresh voice would bring more from certain players, and those who have witnessed Jaissle’s early sessions say that much has been evident.

One of the key takeaways has been a rule that, in certain zones of the pitch, only forward passes are allowed. If the ball goes sideways or backwards, Jaissle will stop play and penalise the offending team. Against Valencia, the likes of Sean Steur, in particular, adhered to that instruction. The new Dutch midfielder, 18, plays far older. He looks ready to be a starter but may have to wait. Jaissle wants former Tottenham man Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, 31, to anchor his midfield and a deal with Marseille should progress in the coming days.

Howe, of course, also wanted to play front-foot football. Having the tools to do so is a different matter entirely, as the former manager found last season in a world without Alexander Isak. But talk of the club’s past - its glories and its failings - is not being entertained by those who are charged with shaping its future, including sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson.

There is great excitement, internally, at the pace of a front three including Anthony Elanga, William Osula and new signing Bazoumana Toure, the Ivory Coast winger who was electric in the second half here. Like Steur, he looks a real find.

Elanga is one of those of whom big things are expected on the back of a poor debut season and, before being stretchered off after a horror challenge that saw Valencia skipper Gaya red carded, he was the pick for Newcastle. The winger, confirmed Jaissle, has escaped serious injury.

He has laid down the law in training, imposing a rule not to pass the ball sideways or backwards in certain drills

Yoane Wissa scored both goals and there is hope that, free of the knee injury that ruined his first season, he will perform to a level that will come close to justifying last summer’s £55m outlay.

But the X-factor, insist the hierarchy, will be Jaissle. They are unlikely to say anything else about their first appointment, and this honeymoon period is not even a week old. Still, there is absolute conviction among insiders when talking about the 38-year-old. His interview was so compelling, we are told, that senior staff wanted to follow him out of the building and offer him the job on the spot. Chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan was among those to speak to Jaissle and he very quickly gave his seal of approval.

There is a feeling among the decision-makers that a young manager with no Premier League baggage or previous domestic allegiances will be afforded patience by supporters. He will no doubt need it. Unless, that is, he really can pull rabbits from hats.

Sports.title: Defiant David Sullivan attends West Ham's Carabao Cup victory over Portsmouth after claiming he was being 'bullied' into not watching it amid sexual misconduct allegations
Sports.content:
Defiant David Sullivan attends West Ham's Carabao Cup victory over Portsmouth after claiming he was being 'bullied' into not watching it amid sexual misconduct allegations

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

David Sullivan emerged to take his seat, cloaked in a thick black bomber jacket. Hardly attire befitting the 28-degree sunshine blazing down on the London Stadium but, as Sullivan has made clear of late, he's not too interested in reading the room.

The stadiums operators told West Ham they didn't want him here because they were worried about fan unrest. The club's own fan advisory board said his presence would cause 'offence and upset'.

Sullivan remains the club's largest shareholder but resigned as co-chair in June amid allegations of sexual misconduct, which he strongly denies, and no longer controls the day-to-day running of the club.

This is, after all, supposed to be the fresh start that West Ham need. It's taken relegation to the Championship and boardroom scandal for them to get it but after years of rotten decline this was, at long last, meant to be it and a gentle stroll into the second round of the Carabao Cup under the afternoon sun should be the ideal way to begin.

Everyone should be talking about how Jarrod Bowen, the loyal captain who stuck with the club, scored one and set up another for Taty Castellanos and showed the kind of quality that will see them as one of the favourites to go back up regardless of how clumsily they played in the first half. Or of the impressive displays of youngsters Lewis Orford and especially Mohamadou Kante in a 3-1 win over Portsmouth.

And yet how can the club make a clean break when the man so many supporters hold responsible for their plight, and against whose ownership they have long protested, was so keen to ignore all that advice.

David Sullivan takes his seat at the London Stadium for West Ham's game with Portsmouth

West Ham came from behind to beat Portsmouth 3-1 in the Carabao Cup first round

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Friday that Sullivan felt he was being 'bullied' by 'keyboard warriors' into staying away. He was concerned about the lack of transfer activity, now that he's no longer the man signing the cheques.

The club have so far turned the loan signing of youngster Keiber Lamadrid permanent and snapped up Joel Veltman, who came on for his debut, on a free from Brighton despite selling Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville for a combined £150million. Why should anyone be able to tell him he can't watch the club he supports?

Not one for reading the room.

Many behind the scenes at West Ham were shocked he planned to attend. Daily Mail Sport knew of one staff member who decided not to come due to the 'circus' of it all.

For Nuno Espirito Santo, at least, it was business as usual. 'We are focused on what happens on the pitch,' he said. 'The noise that comes from outside cannot distract us at all. We are going to find a lot of noise. We focus on the game, do their job, and they did it well.'

The last time Sullivan was here, the final game of the season against Leeds when West Ham's relegation to the Championship was confirmed, he did not stay until the end. Fans pelted him with abuse and he left before full-time.

He made it all the way this time. For all the worries that his attendance might turn the place toxic, he sat there - alongside the vice president of West Ham Women Mickey Cornwell - unperturbed and unpestered. The first boos of the afternoon were not even in his direction but at a hydration break during the first half while the PA system played The Bouncer by Kicks Like a Mule. The burly bloke sat next to Sullivan throughout the game looked like he just might.

If anything, the fans acted as if he wasn't even there. Daily Mail Sport was outside the directors' entrance in September when thousands gathered outside to protest against Sullivan's ownership. Even though his expected attendance had been well-publicised, none bothered this time.

The only chant came on 63 minutes when, coasting at 3-1 up, the fans rose in unison to the chant of: 'Stand up if you hate the board'. Sullivan, to be fair, is not even on it these days. He remains the leading shareholder, although former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley would like to change that.

Sullivan was sat alongside the vice president of West Ham Women, Mickey Cornwell

Sullivan, with Karren Brady in 1993, resigned as West Ham's co-chair in June ahead of the airing of an investigation in which seven women accused Sullivan of predatory behaviour

The fans were too busy trying to make that fresh start. Before kick-off, a clock on the big screen displayed a 'countdown to walkout'. It meant the players, of course, but this place has seen more than its fair share of exoduses in recent years.

Not this time. For the first round of the League Cup, the London Stadium was impressively full. Forever Blowing Bubbles echoed so loudly around the place that a West Ham-supporting member of the press pack turned and grinned: 'Not bad for a Championship side'.

In fact, it was the travelling Portsmouth fans who took it upon themselves to make the first move. 'You sold your soul for this s***hole,' erupted from the away end after four minutes.

If there was going to be a moment when it turned foul, it was when Adrian Segecic long-range effort deflected off the perennially unfortunate Max Kilman to give Portsmouth a deserved lead.

Nuno Espirito Santo's side, to their credit, didn't need long to turn it around. Kante produced some marvellous skill down the left before crossing to an unmarked Castellanos for the equaliser before Bowen curled a beauty from outside the box to put West Ham in front.

Sullivan remained in his seat and clapped. He did so again after half-time when Castellanos nodded in Bowen's cross and, once more, at full-time. As the whistle blew, he stood up, grabbed his jacket, and left the room. Regardless of the advice, you suspect he'll be back.

Sports.title: West Ham and Tottenham agree £5m fee for Manor Solomon, Barcelona to table new bid for Man City's Rodri - and Southampton eye move for Man United youngster: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Everton target the Cherry on top

Everton have added Bournemouth winger Marcus Tavernier to their list of potential wing options this summer.

The 27-year-old is valued around £35m-£40m by Bournemouth.

Everton have also checked on Galatasaray's Baris Yilmaz and Crystal Palace's Brennan Johnson among others.

Everton and Palace discuss McNeil-Johnson swap

Everton and Crystal Palace are in discussions over a potential swap deal between Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson.

Everton and Crystal Palace are in discussions over a potential swap deal between Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson

McNeil was left upset after a move to Palace fell through in January while Johnson has been struggling to find his form since joining in a £35million deal from Tottenham also in the winter window.

The 25-year-old hasn't managed a single goal in his 18 appearances since joining the Eagles.

He has also failed to earn a starting berth, and a trial as a right-wing back under former manager Oliver Glasner failed to trigger improvement. However, David Moyes is a long-term admirer.

McNeil rediscovered form after February but wants more regular starts.

Solomon fee agreed

West Ham and Tottenham have agreed a deal for Manor Solomon at £5million plus add-ons for the 27-year-old winger.

He is expected to undergo his medical over the next 48 hours.

Loan star Ronald Araujo to check in at Liverpool

Ronald Araujo will have a medical at Liverpool on Sunday ahead of completing his loan with option to buy from Barcelona.

Ronald Araujo will have a medical at Liverpool on Sunday ahead of a loan with option to buy

The fee on the option to buy for the 27-year-old defender is £47million.

Araujo is preparing to travel to link up with Liverpool ahead of signing his contract and meeting his new teammates tomorrow.

The Uruguay international gives Liverpool experience and vital defensive cover as he is able to play at centre-back and right-back.

Araujo wanted to go because after talks with coach Hansi Flick it was apparent he would not be guaranteed regular starts and he believes he will find greater opportunity to do so under Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

The Spanish champions are working to offload a number of players as they look to upgrade their squad. They are focused on signing Rodri from Manchester City and still want to strengthen their own centre-back options and at striker.

Araujo will say farewell to Barcelona teammates today prior to heading for Merseyside on Sunday.

Liverpool remain in talks for Paris Saint-Germain pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Full story

Forest on cusp of £36m Diomande move

Nottingham Forest are closing on a £36million deal for Sporting Lisbon centre-back Ousmane Diomande.

The proposed transfer looked to be off last week but a series of conversations have ironed out differences and the 22-year-old Ivory Coast international is due to travel over tomorrow ahead of undergoing a medical.

Forest have a five-year contract in place for the defender.

Forest centre-back Nikola Milenkovic is an option being considered by Juventus while Murillo also has interest from other clubs.

Nottingham Forest are closing on a £36m deal for Sporting centre back Ousmane Diomande

Barca set to table new Rodri bid

Barcelona are preparing a new bid for Manchester City midfielder Rodri after their initial £38million offer plus bonuses was dismissed.

City want £68million for the 30-year-old Spain captain.

Barca are looking to find moves for a number of players including Marc Casado, Roony Bardghji, Hector Fort, Alvaro Cortes, Tommy Marques, Ferran Torres, who is bound for Paris St Germain and Ronald Araujo who is off to Liverpool.

Hammers re-enter Solomon talks

West Ham have revived talks with Tottenham over a deal for winger Manor Solomon.

Talks initially broke down over bonuses due if West Ham were promoted which the Championship side thought were unreasonable but the clubs are working towards a £10million agreement.

Saints eye Man United youngster Kamason

Manchester United full-back Jaydan Kamason is wanted by Southampton.

The Championship side would like the 19-year-old England youth international on a permanent transfer and he is also receiving enquiries from others wanting him on loan.

Preston North End, Blackburn Rovers, Bristol City and Sheffield Wednesday have shown interest in the right-back while there are clubs abroad keen to take him.

Kamason though has a lot of admirers at Old Trafford. He was one of the academy players who excelled in the opening games of United's pre-season, particularly in the 5-0 win over Rosenborg.

He was the first player to sign scholarship forms at United after coming through the club's Emerging Talent Programme, which he joined at 10, while playing for grassroots team Stockport Vikings.

United have yet to decide on plans for his development but he looks likely to stay around Michael Carrick's squad until January.

Goalkeeper Radek Vítek has completed his move to Middlesbrough on a permanent transfer from United in a deal worth up to £14million.

Jaydan Kamason has excelled in pre-season games for United and has plenty of admirers

Geronimo Rulli medical at Man City

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is due to undergo a medical at Manchester City on Monday after the clubs agreed a £1.75million deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45million.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Atletico's Ruggeri to join Villa for £16million

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri has agreed to join Aston Villa. The 24-year-old Italian will cost £16million plus add-ons.

His transfer will help pave the way for Atletico to bid for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

The Argentine centre-back is also among names being considered by Barcelona but Atletico coach Diego Simeone hopes to convince his compatriot if they can agree on terms.

Matteo Ruggeri's move should pave the way for Cristian Romero to join Atletico Madrid

Facundo Buonanotte leaves Brighton for Elche

Brighton midfielder Facundo Buonanotte has joined La Liga side Elche on a season-long loan.

The 21-year-old was on loan at two different Premier League clubs last season, spending the first half with Chelsea before joining Leeds in the second half of the campaign.

Sheffield Wednesday chase Liverpool star Scanlon

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is wanted on loan by Sheffield Wednesday.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff City and they are keen to take him back too.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and is attracting a number of enquiries but League One Wednesday, who play Bolton in the Carabao Cup today, are making a concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick provides Mason Mount injury update after Man United star hobbled off just 20 minutes into pre-season draw against PSG - sparking fears over team's midfield options
Sports.content:
Mason Mount was forced off with an injury during Manchester United's friendly against Paris Saint-Germain, although United boss Michael Carrick was quick to assuage any fears that it could be a long-term issue.

The 27-year-old midfielder has been one of United's standout performers in pre-season, but his latest appearance was cut short after he was substituted just 20 minutes into the match in Gothenburg and replaced by Tyler Fletcher.

Mount spoke to three members of the medical staff before heading down the tunnel and appeared to be experiencing a problem with his foot. He was able to jog off when his number was shown and was later moving well when heading to board the team bus, with Carrick confirming the move had been precautionary.

'He got kicked,' Carrick said after the final whistle. 'We just wanted to be careful and look after him. We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.'

Carrick's comments will come as a welcome boost for United ahead of the new season, which begins in two weeks time.

United, who qualified for the Champions League with their third-place finish last term, kick off their campaign away at newly-promoted Hull. They then host Ipswich and travel to Everton before Old Trafford stages the Manchester derby on September 13.

The midfielder has been one of United's standout performers in pre-season, but his latest appearance was cut short after he was substituted just 20 minutes into the match

Mount spoke to three members of the medical staff before heading down the tunnel and appeared to be experiencing a problem with his foot

Mount, who joined United from Chelsea in a £60million deal in 2023, has struggled with injuries during his time at the club, making 72 appearances across three seasons.

Of the three seasons he has been at United, he made the most top-flight appearances last term with 23, averaging just 44 minutes per game.

In Sweden, United drew 1-1 to United fell behind in the second minute when 18-year-old striker Ibrahim Mbaye buried his chance at the far post.

Bryan Mbeumo then levelled the scoring half an hour later. Amad Diallo won the ball and carried it forward before feeding Mbeumo to the left of the box, with the Cameroonian burying his shot into the far corner.

Neither side could find a winner after the break as the match finished 1-1.

Sports.title: Man United flop Antony is SENT OFF as pre-season friendly between Bournemouth and Real Betis descends into a brawl - with Cherries star also seeing red
Sports.content:
Man United flop Antony is SENT OFF as pre-season friendly between Bournemouth and Real Betis descends into a brawl - with Cherries star also seeing red

Bournemouth's Alex Scott and former Man United winger Antony were shown red cards after a brawl during the Cherries' pre-season friendly with Real Betis.

Players from both sides clashed in the closing stages of the first half at the Benito Villamarin Stadium in Seville.

Real Betis' Nelson Deossa fired a ball at Bafode Diakite from close range after the Bournemouth defender fouled him on the wing.

Deossa's action resulted in the forward being shown a yellow card by the referee but Bournemouth players raced over to make their feelings known.

While most players jogged towards the incident, Real Betis winger Antony was seen sprinting to become involved and was seen pushing two Bournemouth players.

The Brazilian was then confronted by Scott, who was seen pushing Antony away and pointing at the winger.

‘Tangana’ en el Real Betis-Bournemouth que acaba con las expulsiones directas de Antony y Scott.



Surrealista. pic.twitter.com/yAsIWOzdAP — Gonzalo Tortosa (@GonzaloTortosa) August 8, 2026

Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Real Betis' Antony were sent off after a clash during their pre-season friendly

Former Man United winger Antony caused a confrontation between the two teams on the stroke of half-time

Scott was shown a red card for his involvement after he was seen pushing Antony away

Antony was then seen raising his arms and pushing Scott, with the Bournemouth midfielder moving away from the incident.

The referee ultimately opted to punish both Antony and Scott for the clash, with the pair shown red cards on the stroke of half-time.

The decision came despite Antony, who left Man United for Real Betis last summer, appearing to have been the main aggressor as tempers flared between the two sides.

Bournemouth had led the friendly 1-0 at the time, with new Cherries boss Marco Rose seeing his side go ahead through Marcus Tavernier in the 41st minute.

The teams exchanged quick-fire goals in the second half with Isco temporarily drawing the hosts level, before Evanilson restored Bournemouth's lead on the hour mark.

Real Betis equalised for the second time late on through former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals.

The match was Bournemouth's penultimate pre-season fixture ahead of the new season.

Bournemouth will face German opposition in Mainz next Saturday, before turning their attentions to their season opener against Man City on August 23.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
