World.title: FIFA Defends Gianni Infantino Amid Leadership Crisis
World.content:
FIFA has accused critics of waging a “concerted and ongoing effort” to undermine the organization and its president, Gianni Infantino, as the crisis surrounding his leadership continues to deepen. The governing body issued a strongly worded statement Saturday defending Infantino following the collapse of a controversial proposal to bring private investors into FIFA’s World Cup commercial business.

The plan triggered fierce opposition from several major football organizations and has left Infantino facing boycott threats, calls for his resignation and growing questions about his bid for another term as FIFA president. Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, is seeking reelection at the organization’s congress in March 2027. FIFA’s 211 member associations will ultimately decide whether he remains in office.

European football’s governing body UEFA has emerged as one of his strongest critics. Despite FIFA abandoning the private investment proposal, UEFA has said the decision alone is not enough to restore confidence in Infantino’s leadership. The dispute has escalated to the point that European football officials have threatened to boycott FIFA competitions, including World Cups.

New Allegations Add to Pressure

Infantino faced another controversy Friday after The Telegraph reported allegations involving his time as UEFA general secretary between 2009 and 2016. The British newspaper alleged that Infantino used his influence to help secure the promotion of a female UEFA employee with whom he was reportedly involved in a personal relationship.

Infantino has categorically denied the allegations. The Telegraph also reported that the employee later received a six-figure payment when she left UEFA, along with approximately €50,000 ($57,800) toward an MBA program. UEFA has acknowledged that a payment was made to the former employee and that expenses connected with an MBA program were also covered.

FIFA did not specifically identify the Telegraph report in its Saturday statement but pushed back strongly against recent coverage surrounding its president. “Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its president,” the organization said. FIFA added that speculation and insinuation should not be treated as fact and said it would challenge inaccurate or misleading reporting.

FIFA Warns Against Attempts to Remove Infantino

FIFA also emphasized that any effort to replace Infantino must follow the organization’s statutes and established election procedures. “Those who do not have the support of FIFA’s Member Associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA’s established democratic processes,” the organization said.

FIFA’s leadership reaffirmed its support for Infantino during a crisis meeting in Morocco earlier this week. The organization also apologized to its 211 member associations for mistakes in the way the private investment proposal was handled, acknowledging that members should have been more involved in the process.

That apology has done little to settle the dispute. UEFA has said it has lost confidence in Infantino, while Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness went further Friday and publicly called for him to resign. Klaveness, one of Infantino’s most outspoken critics in international football, said he no longer has the institutional trust necessary to lead FIFA.

Her name has also been mentioned as a possible future candidate for the FIFA presidency, although she has played down speculation about running.

Infantino Retains Support Outside Europe

Despite the growing pressure in Europe, Infantino continues to receive significant backing elsewhere. The Confederation of African Football has publicly supported his leadership, while South American governing body Conmebol has rejected attempts to remove him outside FIFA’s established electoral process.

Infantino traveled to Cali, Colombia, on Friday for the inauguration of newly elected right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella, where Conmebol president Alejandro Domínguez reiterated his support. Domínguez said Infantino’s work at FIFA should not be ignored and called for disagreements within world football to be resolved through dialogue.

The competing statements highlight a widening divide within international football ahead of the 2027 FIFA presidential election. For years, Infantino appeared to be heading toward another term with relatively little resistance. The collapse of the private investment plan and the increasingly public confrontation between FIFA and UEFA have now turned what once looked like a straightforward reelection campaign into one of the most serious leadership crises of his decade in charge.

World.title: Costa Rica Reports Renewed Increase in COVID-19 Cases
World.content:
COVID-19 has once again become the most widely circulating respiratory virus detected in Costa Rica, as health officials urge residents to take basic precautions amid an increase in cases and hospitalizations. The latest epidemiological surveillance places COVID-19 ahead of rhinovirus and parainfluenza among respiratory viruses currently circulating here.

During epidemiological week 29, covering July 13 through July 19, Costa Rica recorded 126 confirmed COVID-19 cases, up from 94 the previous week. That represents an increase of about 34%. Hospitalizations also climbed, with 29 COVID-19 patients receiving hospital care compared with 18 the previous week, an increase of roughly 56%. Five deaths associated with COVID-19 were reported during the same epidemiological week.

The figures remain far below the levels Costa Rica experienced during the height of the pandemic, and there is currently no national health alert for respiratory illnesses. However, the change in circulation has prompted renewed attention as several respiratory viruses spread simultaneously.

Costa Rica has recorded more than 771,000 cases of respiratory illness so far this year, a broader figure that includes illnesses caused by multiple viruses rather than COVID-19 alone. Children, older adults and people with chronic health conditions remain among those considered most vulnerable to complications from respiratory infections.

Health authorities are recommending many of the familiar measures used to reduce respiratory infections: keeping vaccinations current, washing hands regularly, covering coughs and sneezes and choosing well-ventilated spaces when possible. People experiencing respiratory symptoms are also being encouraged to avoid crowded activities and limit close contact with vulnerable relatives or friends until they recover.

The renewed circulation of COVID-19 comes during Costa Rica’s rainy season, when respiratory illnesses can become more noticeable as people spend more time indoors and several viruses circulate at the same time. For residents and travelers, the latest numbers do not signal a return to pandemic-era restrictions. There have been no announcements of renewed mask mandates, travel requirements or widespread restrictions connected to the current increase.

Instead, the emphasis remains on individual precautions, particularly for people at greater risk of serious illness. Health officials continue to monitor COVID-19 alongside influenza, rhinovirus, parainfluenza and other respiratory illnesses to identify changes in circulation and hospital demand.

World.title: Why the Cincinnati Open Is the Last Major Test Before the US Open
World.content:
The Cincinnati Open begins opening its grounds to fans this weekend, but for the players arriving in Mason, Ohio, the tournament carries considerably more weight than another stop on the summer schedule. Cincinnati is the final ATP Masters 1000 and WTA 1000 tournament before the US Open, making the next two weeks one of the clearest tests of who is ready to contend in New York and who still has work to do.



Qualifying begins August 11 at the Lindner Family Tennis Center, followed by the men’s and women’s main draws on August 13. The Cincinnati singles finals will be played August 23. Exactly one week later, on August 30, the US Open singles main draws begin in New York. That short turnaround is what gives Cincinnati its importance.

Players who make deep runs will arrive at Flushing Meadows with confidence, match fitness and proof that their games are working on North American hard courts. Those struggling with injuries, form or the transition from other surfaces have little time left to make adjustments.

Cincinnati Offers a Grand Slam-Level Test

Cincinnati is not a Grand Slam, but the quality of competition makes it one of the closest things players will encounter before New York. The men’s tournament is an ATP Masters 1000 event and the women’s competition carries WTA 1000 status. Both feature 96-player singles draws filled with many of the highest-ranked players in the world.

A Masters 1000 title on the men’s side is worth 1,000 ranking points, while the tournament also offers substantial ranking opportunities throughout the draw. But Cincinnati’s value goes beyond points.

Players will face many of the same opponents they could encounter a week later at the US Open, often under demanding summer conditions. Long matches, heat, humidity and repeated days of competition provide a useful indication of who is physically prepared for a two-week Grand Slam.

It also gives players another chance to solve problems that became apparent earlier in the North American hard-court season. A serve that was effective on another surface may not produce the same results. A player struggling to defend a second serve or finish short balls has very little time remaining to correct those weaknesses.

By Cincinnati, experimentation begins to give way to urgency.

Hard Courts Change the Equation

The transition to North American hard courts is particularly important because the US Open rewards a different combination of skills than the European clay and grass seasons that dominate the preceding months. Movement changes. Points can develop more quickly. First serves and returns become increasingly important, and players who can take control of the baseline early are often rewarded.

For players who built much of their season on clay, Cincinnati can provide an especially revealing test. That makes the tournament worth watching closely for Latin American tennis fans. Brazil’s João Fonseca, Argentina’s Francisco Cerúndolo, Sebastián Báez and Tomás Martín Etcheverry, Peru’s Ignacio Buse and Chile’s Alejandro Tabilo are among the players from the region heading into the Cincinnati period with the US Open approaching.

Colombia’s Camila Osorio leads the Latin American presence on the women’s side, with other players from the region attempting to reach the main draw through qualifying. The question for each is not simply how far they can advance in Ohio. Cincinnati will provide another measure of how well their games are translating to the surface they will encounter in New York.

Ranking Points Matter, But So Does the Draw

Cincinnati can also change a player’s position heading into the final Grand Slam of the season. A deep run at a 1000-level tournament can produce a substantial rankings boost, particularly for players clustered closely together in the standings. That matters because rankings help determine seedings and ultimately influence the path a player may face through a major tournament.

For someone near one of those dividing lines, a strong Cincinnati performance can have consequences beyond the tournament itself. The difference between being seeded and unseeded at a Grand Slam can mean avoiding one of the world’s highest-ranked players in the opening rounds.

Even for players whose US Open position is already secure, Cincinnati provides something equally valuable: matches against elite opposition. There is little substitute for facing one of the world’s best players shortly before a Grand Slam.

Fitness Will Be Closely Watched

Cincinnati will also offer important clues about injuries and fatigue. The professional tennis calendar leaves little recovery time during the summer. Players move from Europe to North America and then through a series of hard-court tournaments before reaching New York. Some arrive in Cincinnati searching for matches. Others arrive needing rest. Finding the balance is difficult.

A player eliminated early may lose an opportunity to build match rhythm before the US Open. A player who reaches the Cincinnati final could play through August 23 and then have only seven days before the first Sunday of singles competition in New York. That creates difficult decisions for players dealing with even relatively minor physical problems.

The withdrawal of defending men’s champion Carlos Alcaraz because of a wrist injury is a reminder of how quickly the complexion of the tournament can change at this point in the season. Others will arrive trying to manage their workloads while still pursuing one of the biggest titles available outside the Grand Slams.

What Cincinnati Can Tell Us

Tournament results alone will not predict the US Open. Tennis history is filled with players who struggled in their final warm-up tournament and then found their best form at a Grand Slam. Others have arrived in New York carrying a long winning streak only to lose early.

Still, several things will be worth watching in Cincinnati. How players move after long matches. Whether their first serves remain effective late in sets. How aggressively they return. Whether they can maintain their level through consecutive days of competition. And perhaps most importantly, how comfortable they look.

By the middle of August, there are few opportunities remaining to completely rebuild a game before the US Open. Cincinnati is where many of those questions begin to receive answers. The tournament’s qualifying rounds start August 11, with main-draw play beginning August 13 and the singles finals scheduled for August 23.

The US Open begins its Fan Week and qualifying activities the same day Cincinnati crowns its champions, before the main singles draws start August 30. For tennis fans here in Costa Rica and across Latin America, that makes Cincinnati much more than a warm-up event. It is the last major checkpoint before the tennis world turns its attention to New York.

World.title: Costa Rica Warns Pet Owners After Rabies Kills Cattle in Golfito
World.content:
A rabies outbreak that killed three cattle in southern Costa Rica has prompted renewed warnings for ranchers and pet owners to keep animals vaccinated, particularly in areas where vampire bats can transmit the virus. The latest outbreak was found in Pilón, in the area around Pavones, Golfito. The affected farm was placed under quarantine, and all 165 cattle on the property were ordered vaccinated as part of efforts to prevent further spread.

People who had direct contact with the infected animals are also receiving preventive treatment. The Golfito outbreak brings the number of reported paralytic bovine rabies outbreaks in Costa Rica to five so far in 2026. Cases have been recorded in Upala, Cañas, Osa and Golfito, reinforcing concern in rural areas where cattle and wildlife frequently come into contact.

The virus affecting cattle in these outbreaks is primarily transmitted by vampire bats, particularly Desmodus rotundus, a species that feeds on blood. Infected bats can bite the same animal repeatedly over several nights, allowing the virus to enter the animal’s body if it has not been vaccinated.

For cattle, rabies often appears differently than the aggressive form commonly associated with infected dogs. Bovine cases typically develop what is known as paralytic or “dumb” rabies. Early signs can include weakness in the rear legs, difficulty walking and problems remaining upright. As the disease advances, animals may develop paralysis of the tail and jaw, excessive salivation, difficulty swallowing and eventually become unable to stand.

The disease is fatal once it develops. The concern extends beyond cattle. Veterinary specialists are urging residents in affected and rabies-prone areas to make sure dogs and cats are current on their annual rabies vaccinations. Cats can face particular exposure because they sometimes hunt bats that enter homes, barns or nearby buildings. An unvaccinated dog or cat that contracts rabies can then expose people through bites, scratches or saliva.

Those in the area are also being warned not to handle bats, whether they appear healthy, injured or dead. Anyone bitten by a bat or who believes they may have had direct contact with one should seek medical attention immediately rather than waiting for symptoms to develop. Preventive treatment is most effective when started before the virus reaches the nervous system.

Costa Rica is home to a large diversity of bat species, and the current warning should not be seen as a reason to harm them. Most bats play important roles in the ecosystem by eating insects, spreading seeds and pollinating plants. The concern surrounding bovine rabies is focused primarily on blood-feeding vampire bats and the possibility of infected animals passing the virus to livestock or domestic animals.

Current control efforts emphasize vaccination rather than widespread killing of bats. Livestock in affected areas can be vaccinated, domestic animals kept current on their shots, and suspected cases reported quickly so veterinary teams can investigate. Ranchers are being told to watch cattle closely for neurological symptoms and to avoid handling animals showing unexplained paralysis, excessive salivation, coordination problems or sudden changes in behavior.

Suspected animals should not be moved, and carcasses should not be removed or handled without guidance from animal health personnel. The Golfito outbreak is particularly noteworthy in Costa Rica’s southern area, where cattle farms overlap with extensive forest and wildlife habitat.

Pavones is better known internationally for its beaches and surfing, but much of the surrounding canton remains rural, with farms, forests and small communities spread across a large area. There has been no indication that the outbreak poses a general threat to visitors traveling to Pavones or Golfito. The practical concern is direct contact with infected animals or bats, particularly for ranchers, veterinarians, farm workers and people living with unvaccinated pets in affected areas.

For most people the best protection is to keep dogs, cats and livestock vaccinated and report animals showing unusual neurological symptoms. This new warning comes as Costa Rica balances two important priorities: protecting livestock and public health while recognizing the ecological importance of bats in controlling insects, pollinating plants and dispersing seeds throughout Costa Rica’s ecosystems.

World.title: Belize @45 Workshop Explores Sovereignty and Nationhood
World.content:
Belize @45 Workshop Explores Sovereignty and Nationhood

By Zoila Palma: The Belize @45 Workshop, a three-day professional development training, was held from August 5 to 7, 2026, bringing together educators from across the country to examine what Belize’s independence really means.

The training was a collaborative effort of the Institute for Social and Cultural Research (ISCR), the Belize Archives and Records Service (BARS), the Ministry of Education, Culture, Science & Technology (MOECST), specifically Ms. Ruby Reyes of the Belizean Studies Curriculum and Assessment Unit, the George Price Centre for Peace and Development, the University of Belize, and Galen University.

During the training, historian and diplomat Assad Shoman challenged educators to reflect on the “role of teachers and students in shaping Belize’s future.”

The event included virtual sessions and an in-person learning session at the George Price Centre for Peace and Development in Belmopan, equipping educators with new tools and perspectives to bring Belize’s history and independence journey to life for students.

Organizers emphasized that Belize’s independence is not simply an achievement of the past, but an ongoing process, underscoring the message: “Independence is the beginning!

World.title: Belizeans Travel Across U.S. for Passport and Nationality Services at Evanston Diaspora Hub
World.content:
Belizeans Travel Across U.S. for Passport and Nationality Services at Evanston Diaspora Hub

By Zoila Palma: Belizeans from across the Chicago area and several other parts of the United States travelled to Evanston this weekend to access passport and nationality services brought directly to the diaspora by Belize’s Ministry of Immigration, Governance and Labour.

The three-day Evanston Diaspora Hub runs from August 7 to 9. The event provides passport and nationality services, including first-time and renewal passport applications, as well as applications for Belizean nationality by descent.

The ministry says that the outreach provides a more convenient way to complete important documentation without having to travel to Belize. Belizean passport applicants are required to appear in person at an Immigration Office in Belize or at a designated Belizean diplomatic or consular mission, making mobile outreach efforts particularly valuable for Belizeans living far from those locations.

The Evanston hub also highlighted the strong community ties among Belizeans living in the United States. Some Chicago-area residents noted that they have built a vibrant Belizean community and are preparing to host a fundraiser on Saturday to provide scholarships to 14 Belizean-American students attending school.

Belize’s Ambassador to the United States, H.E. Nestor E. Mendez, visited the hub alongside Belize’s Ambassador for Diaspora Relations, Sandhya Murphy, as officials engaged with Belizeans accessing the services.

The Evanston initiative follows other diaspora outreach efforts by the Government of Belize in the United States. Earlier this year, approximately 230 passports and 17 nationality certificates were delivered to Belizeans abroad during another outreach initiative, reflecting continued demand for documentation services within Belizean communities across the United States.

World.title: Belizeans travel from across the United States to Evanston, Chicago, for immigration services at Diaspora Hub
World.content:
Belizeans travel from across the United States to Evanston, Chicago, for immigration services at Diaspora Hub

By Hugh O’Brien: Belizeans from across the Chicago area and the larger United States, including Texas, Washington and Colorado, travelled to Evanston this weekend to access passport and nationality services being offerred directly to the diaspora by Belize’s Ministry of Immigration, Governance and Labour.

The Diaspora Mobile Hub, being held from August 7 to 9, is providing Belizeans living in the United States with an opportunity to complete nationality and passport applications without having to travel to Belize or wait for an appointment at a designated Belizean diplomatic or consular mission.

While many of those attending came from Evanston, Chicago and surrounding communities, others travelled hundreds or even thousands of miles to take advantage of the outreach initiative. Several Belizeans from the Dallas area made the journey to Evanston to submit applications and complete other documentation processes.

In a public statement posted on its Facebook page, the Ministry said “Some visitors came to renew their Belizean passports, while others submitted first-time passport applications. Families also visited the hub to apply for Belizean nationality by descent, allowing eligible children and other descendants born outside Belize to formally establish their Belizean nationality.”

The Ministry said that these services are being provided through the Nationality and Passports Department as part of the Ministry’s broader effort to bring essential government services closer to Belizeans living abroad.

“For members of the diaspora, having services available in a U.S. city can significantly reduce the time, cost and logistical challenges associated with completing important documentation. Belizean passport applicants are required to appear in person at an Immigration Office in Belize or at a designated Belizean diplomatic or consular mission.”

For this reason, according to the Ministry, Evanston became a destination this weekend not only for Belizeans living in Illinois, but also for members of the diaspora who travelled from across the United States.

“For some families, the visit was simply about renewing a passport and maintaining the ability to travel using Belizean documentation. For others, particularly parents seeking nationality by descent for their children, the process represented another way of passing their connection to Belize from one generation to the next,” said the Ministry.

Belize’s Ambassador to the United States, H.E. Nestor E. Mendez, attended the Ministry’s immigration outreach alongside Belize’s Ambassador for Diaspora Relations, Sandhya Murphy.

Belizean nationality by descent is available to qualifying persons born outside Belize based on Belizean parentage.

The Evanston Diaspora Mobile Hub continues will conclude on Sunday, August 9.

World.title: Halo BPO sweetens the deal: $10 an hour plus commission for home based sales agents
World.content:
Halo BPO sweetens the deal: $10 an hour plus commission for home based sales agents

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Halo BPO is back on the hiring trail, and the terms have improved. The company’s latest recruitment drive for work from home sales agents offers $9.00 BZD per hour during training, rising to $10.00 BZD per hour after training, plus commission and bonuses, with pay issued weekly, an upgrade on the $8.50 flat rate advertised earlier this month.

The role is full time outbound sales, done entirely from home anywhere in Belize. The qualifying bar has risen alongside the pay: applicants now need two or more years of sales experience, and credit repair experience is listed as a plus, suggesting the campaign involves the credit services market.

The technical requirement is the other significant change. Home internet must deliver at least 85 Mbps download and 45 Mbps upload, a specification that in practice points to fibre-grade service, so applicants should run a speed test before applying.

For experienced sellers with strong connections, the package is among the more competitive remote offers advertised locally: guaranteed hourly pay, weekly payout, and commission upside on top.

Applications go to [email protected], and the standing instruction applies: include your full name in the email subject line.

World.title: The weekend keeps its promise: sunshine across Belize
World.content:
The weekend keeps its promise: sunshine across Belize

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The forecast made the promise on Friday, and Saturday is delivering it in full. Mainly fair weather conditions prevail across Belize, with sunshine overhead, gentle seas, and inland heat reaching 95 degrees, and Sunday is set to repeat the performance.

According to the National Meteorological Service, skies will be sunny with a few cloudy spells today and clear to partly cloudy tonight. Showers or thunderstorms will be isolated, with a medium chance of a few more mostly over the Toledo District tonight, the weekend’s lone exception to the fair pattern.

Temperatures along the coast will reach a high of 89 degrees Fahrenheit (32 Celsius) and a low of 82 (28 Celsius). Inland areas will be the hottest in the country, climbing to 95 degrees Fahrenheit (35 Celsius) before dropping to 73 (23 Celsius). In the hills, expect a high of 83 degrees Fahrenheit (28 Celsius) and a cool low of 67 (19 Celsius). With the mercury at 95 inland, the weekend checklist stays simple: water close and shade often.

At sea, conditions remain at their friendliest, with easterly winds of 5 to 15 knots, a light chop, and waves of 2 to 4 feet, fine water for the weekend’s boaters, snorkelers, and fishing trips.

On the tropical front, the calm holds. Tropical cyclone formation is not expected in the region over the next 48 hours.

Looking ahead to Sunday and Sunday night, similar weather conditions are expected to prevail, carrying the sunshine through the full weekend.

Today’s low tides are at 1:06 PM and 11:32 PM, with a high tide at 7:41 PM and another high at 6:11 AM tomorrow. The sun sets this evening at 6:22 PM and rises tomorrow at 5:34 AM. The forecast was issued by forecaster Tareek Matthews.

World.title: Santander clarifies operations following reports of fish kill in Belize River
World.content:
Santander clarifies operations following reports of fish kill in Belize River

By Zoila Palma: On August 7, 2026, Santander Sugar Group (SSG) released a statement clarifying its operations following reports of aquatic life deaths in the Belize River Valley.

The release states that Santander Sugar Group is “deeply saddened by the loss of aquatic life recently reported in the Belize River Valley.” The company said it recognizes the importance of the Belize River to surrounding communities, the environment and Belize as a whole.

Santander said protecting natural resources remains a core principle of its operations. The company explained that it operates under an approved Environmental Compliance Plan and continuously monitors its operations while implementing measures to minimize runoff and protect surrounding waterways.

The company also said it has fully cooperated with the Department of the Environment (DoE) and other relevant government agencies since the incident was reported. According to SSG, the DoE was granted unrestricted access to its facilities and operations to support the ongoing investigation.

Santander further stated that its processing facility is designed to operate as a closed-loop system and does not operate with a continuous process effluent stream returning to the Belize River. The company said it remains committed to providing any additional information or assistance that may be required as authorities continue their investigation.

World.title: Belize City featured in Commonwealth Study
World.content:
Belize City featured in Commonwealth Study

By BBN Staff: Belize City is being featured in a new Commonwealth study examining how cities and local governments can close the urban finance gap and secure sustainable funding for infrastructure and essential services. The city was selected as one of only three case studies highlighted in the research, alongside Kerala State in India and Kigali, Rwanda.

On Wednesday, August 5, Belize City Mayor Bernard Wagner participated in the Commonwealth Local Government Forum’s webinar, “The Urban Finance Gap: Practical Pathways for Local Government Finance across the Commonwealth.” The discussion explored practical approaches to strengthening local government finance, improving resilience and ensuring cities have the resources needed to deliver critical services.

During the webinar, Wagner emphasized that financing infrastructure projects cannot end once construction is completed. He noted that projects such as drainage systems and roads must be designed to withstand changing conditions while also having adequate funding for operation, maintenance and eventual renewal. The Yarborough Pumping Station was highlighted as an example, having proven effective in draining the city’s waterways during flooding but also requiring significant recurring costs for continued operation and maintenance.

The Belize City Council said the city’s inclusion in the study highlights its fiscal administration, innovative approach to municipal finance and experience with its Municipal Bond Programme. It added that closing the urban finance gap will require greater decentralization, sustainable financing frameworks and increased trust in capable local governments to invest in their communities. Belize City’s experience is being presented as an example of what local leadership can achieve despite limited fiscal space.

World.title: Department of the Environment provides update on Fish Kill in the Belize River Valley area
World.content:
Department of the Environment provides update on Fish Kill in the Belize River Valley area

INVESTIGATION INTO THE FISH KILL IN THE BELIZE RIVER VALLEY AREA

Belmopan, Belize. August 7, 2026: The public is hereby informed that, as part of the ongoing investigation into the fish kill in the Belize River Valley area, the Department of the Environment (DOE) has conducted visual observations and water quality assessments from near Banana Bank, upstream of Santander Farms, to the Burrell Boom Village bridge. Significant fish mortality and changes in water conditions were observed particularly along the approximately 17.5-mile stretch between Isabella Bank and Grace Bank. The Department is also assessing discharge points and other activities along and within the vicinity of the river as part of its investigation into the possible source or sources of the event.

On-site water quality testing and sampling have been conducted at various locations along the river. Preliminary field results recorded extremely low levels of dissolved oxygen in areas where significant fish mortality was observed, together with elevated conductivity, chlorophyll-a and turbidity at certain locations. These conditions can adversely affect aquatic life. Samples have been submitted for laboratory analysis to assist in determining the cause of the observed conditions.

As part of the ongoing investigation, the DOE has also collected water samples from the Santander Farms drainage system and at locations downstream for chemical analysis. Fish and sediment samples are also being collected and analysed to assist in determining the cause of the fish mortality and whether contaminants may have contributed to the event.

The Department is additionally reviewing satellite imagery from before and during the event to assess changes in water conditions, land-clearing activities and other factors that may assist in identifying potential contributing sources. Investigations and assessments are also being conducted in relation to other developments, activities and potential discharge points within the wider area.

At this stage, the Department has not determined the source or responsible party associated with the fish kill. The investigation remains ongoing, and any determination will be based on the results of laboratory analyses and the totality of the scientific and technical evidence collected.

The precautionary advisory issued by the Department on August 5, 2026, remains in effect. The public is therefore advised not to consume fish or other aquatic resources from the affected areas and not to use untreated river water for drinking, cooking, food preparation, livestock or pets until further notice. This advisory applies to untreated water taken directly from the river and does not apply to treated potable water supplied by Belize Water Services Limited.

The DOE continues to coordinate with relevant government agencies and other authorities in monitoring the situation and advancing the investigation. The public will be informed as laboratory results and other verified findings become available.

The Department of the Environment remains committed to protecting Belize’s environment, safeguarding our natural resources and public health, and ensuring that all potential sources are thoroughly investigated and that appropriate action is taken where the evidence establishes a breach of Belize’s environmental laws.

END

For More Information Contact: Anthony Mai, Chief Environmental Officer

World.title: Jamaica’s Edwards snatches triple jump gold at World U20 Champs
World.content:
In this March 2026 file photo, Jamaica College star Michael-Andre Edwards displays his gold medal after winning the Class 1 Boys’ triple jump final, with a leap of 16.25m., to close out his Champs career. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

OREGON, USA – Michael Andre Edwards thought he would be able to jump “about 16.80m” but surprised himself with a dramatic final round 17.08m (1.1m/s) leap to snatch the gold medal at the World Athletics Under- 20 Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon.

Edwards, who started slowly, trailed his good friend American Miles Nesmith going into the final round, when he produced the jump of his life on the biggest stage.

After his dramatic win, he said he never expected he would be jumping this far this soon but never thought 17.00m was out of his reach.

He twice bettered his previous personal best of 16.30m set in July, with 16.71m in the fifth round and then his big jump a round later. He joins national under-20 record holder Jaydon Hibbert,17.87m, and James Beckford, 17.29m, as the only Jamaican juniors to jump over 17.00m in the triple jump.

Edwards is also the second Jamaican man to win the triple jump after Hibbert won it in 2022.

This was Jamaica’s first gold of the champions and third medal after Gary Card and Shanoya Douglas won silver medals in their respective 100m finals on Thursday.

Nesmith, who was second to Edwards at the Penn Relays in April, took the silver medal with a personal best 16.79m (1.0m/s) and China’s Zhuoyue Wang was third with 16.36m (0.9m/s).

Edwards, who needed just one jump, 16.00m, to qualify from the prelims, started slowly with a 13.76m (1.4m/s) but qualified for the final with a 16.23m (-0.3m/s) in the third round before he got into second place with 16.71 (0.5m/s) in the fifth round.

-Paul A Reid

World.title: Hurting Jamaica
World.content:
An inflatable obstacle course at the entry fee-free Harmony Beach Park in Montego Bay, St James.

FALMOUTH, Trelawny — Minister of Tourism Edmund Bartlett has criticised people who he says are creating a false impression internationally that Jamaicans are being denied access to the country’s beaches.

Speaking at the 2026 Artisan Village Food Festival in Falmouth on Thursday, Bartlett argued that the facts do not support the narrative being circulated overseas and the false claims are damaging Jamaica’s reputation and costing the Government money to correct.

“We have 70 [public bathing beaches] in Jamaica, all around the island. And of that 70 only 10 of them are paid beaches. And then only five of that you would pay a decent money to go to,” Bartlett said.

“And yet, some of us, when you hear what we say to the international media… you would believe that every beach in Jamaica is just locked off, and that’s not fair to Jamaica. That’s not fair to us,” added Bartlett.

He argued that concerns may arise about access to specific beaches, but insisted that isolated issues should not be used to broad-brush the country.

“So we say, if you have an issue with one, or two, all right, let’s talk about that. Let’s deal with it because everywhere in the world you go, there’s an issue. But we must deal with it and resolve it, and not define ourselves by it,” argued Bartlett.

The tourism minister said the Government has had to invest in advertising and promotional campaigns to counter misinformation in the international media.

“You know as minister of tourism how much trouble I get on international press to go and explain to them that it is not true? Then we have to spend money with advertising agents… to tell them seh nothing nuh go so,” Bartlett said.

He urged Jamaicans to resolve national challenges internally rather than tarnishing the country’s image overseas.

“So we have to help ourselves. Where we have a problem, let us resolve it. Let us see where the difficulties are, talk about it, deal with it at home, solve it at home. And, as Miss Lou seh, ‘Don’t wash your dirty linen abroad,’ because when you believe you are hurting your neighbour, you’re not hurting your neighbour, you’re hurting your country and, in the end, yourself,” Bartlett added.

He lamented what he described as a tendency among some Jamaicans to highlight only the country’s shortcomings.

“Some of us enjoy beating up little Jamaica. Some of us enjoy saying all the negative things about the country, and some people I hear say things like Jamaica refuse to make its people enjoy the beaches. I never hear anything like that,” he said.

Bartlett urged Jamaicans to use the country’s 64th anniversary of Independence to embrace a new conversation and project a more positive image of the nation.

“And as we do that, the second thing I want to concern my mind and to get you into my thoughts on is how it is that we project ourselves as a people and as a country,” Bartlett said.

“The world views us through our own eyes and through our prisms. The world sees us the way we see ourselves, but most importantly, the way we express who we are to the world,” he added.

Bartlett said Jamaica’s 64th Independence anniversary should mark the beginning of a more positive national outlook.

“So, on this 64th birthday, let us resolve to have a new conversation, a new narrative, a positive contribution to ourselves, as together we grow. As we recover from Melissa, we recover stronger and better, and we build this great little piece of rock. In the words of Miss Lou, ‘We little but we tallawah,’” he said.

Official data show Jamaica possesses approximately 1,022 kilometres of coastline, of which approximately 29 per cent (300 kilometres) consists of sandy beaches.

World.title: Potential investors wary as tourism GCT increase looms
World.content:
HERON... I have had calls from a number of investors who have told me point blank that they are concerned

MONTEGO BAY, St James — The Jamaica Hotel and Tourist Association (JHTA) says the uncertainty surrounding the Government’s proposed increase in the general consumption tax (GCT) on the sector is causing concern among potential investors.

According to JHTA President O’Brian Heron, the proposal has left some investors uneasy as they assess their plans for the local tourism industry.

“I have had calls from a number of investors who have told me point blank that they are concerned and they really want us to get this GCT issue resolved as quickly as possible because it does affect their ability, it does affect their excitement and their passion and their trust in the ability to invest in destination Jamaica,” Heron told the Jamaica Observer.

His comments come as tourism stakeholders and Government representatives continue discussions aimed at finding common ground on the proposal to increase the GCT applicable to sections of the sector from 10 per cent to 15 per cent.

“There are concerns; a number of investors are restive at this time and are really waiting to see what the outcome will be of these GCT discussions and negotiations with the Government,” Heron added on the margins of a HEART/NSTA Trust Priority Sector Industry Roundtable with tourism stakeholders on Friday.

The proposed increase was announced as part of the Government’s revenue measures during the 2026-27 Budget Debate, prompting widespread concern across the tourism industry.

According to Heron, the additional tax burden would further compound the challenges the sector is facing as it works to remain viable.

“What we are particularly concerned about is, our industry has been subject to a number of shocks over the years. From COVID-19, on the heels of that we had Hurricane Beryl, then there is Hurricane Melissa, there is increasing oil prices and fuel prices all over, there is significant pressure being borne by the industry right now that is trying to recover… trying to settle insurance claims and this is going to squeeze the industry to a point where we risk our own competitiveness,” added Heron.

He said these concerns prompted the JHTA to approach the Ministry of Finance for discussions on the plan.

“I believe that our focus and our push with ensuring the Government understands the affordability issue and the profitability issue is something we need to remain very strident on, we need to remain very steadfast on,” the JHTA president said.

He told the Observer that some progress was made during a recent meeting with officials of the Ministry of Finance.

“Where we are when we left the conversation with the minister of finance [Fayval Williams] is that we agreed to form a working group to really explore alternative solutions around opportunities to help the Government to meet its fiscal objectives without squeezing the industry to a point of not really being able to be competitive, or to perform,” Heron said.

The JHTA president argued that the tourism industry has consistently made significant contributions to Government revenue and continues to do so.

“The industry is not anti-tax. As a matter of fact, we already pay our fair share of taxes, whether it is through corporate taxes or other statutory taxes that actually exist,” he explained.

“To operate a hotel, we’re also subjected to a number of licences and fees that are renewable every year and come with their own sets of inspections,” Heron said.

World.title: Grand Gala honours Rock resilience
World.content:
Prime Minister Andrew Holness acknowledges the roar of the crowd. Garfield Robinson

As the island’s annual Emancipendence celebrations culminated in grand style on Thursday evening, thousands of Jamaicans draped in black, green and gold descended on the National Stadium with one purpose: To celebrate the nation’s 64th anniversary of nationhood and pay tribute to the unbreakable spirit that has carried the country through triumph and tragedy.

Coming less than a year after the devastation of Hurricane Melissa, one of the most destructive storms in the nation’s history, this year’s Grand Gala carried a deeper significance. Beneath the pageantry, the music, and the fireworks was a quiet but resolute declaration from the Jamaican people: We are still standing.

Throughout the evening, the resilience of a nation took centre stage as generations of entertainers, cultural practitioners, and musicians came together in a dazzling display of Jamaican excellence.

Among the night’s most anticipated moments were the performances from honorees Busy Signal and Wayne Wonder, both of whom reminded patrons why their music continues to occupy a treasured place in the country’s cultural landscape.

Busy Signal delivered an electrifying set, moving effortlessly through crowd favourites such as

Step Out Inna Mi Black, Bumaye, and

Nah Go Jail Again. Yet, it was his stirring performance of

Jamaica Love that became the emotional heartbeat of the night.

As the stadium lights dimmed, the entertainer urged patrons to illuminate the venue with their phone flash lights. In an instant, thousands of tiny lights pierced the darkness, transforming the stadium into what seemed a sea of stars. What followed was less of a performance and more of a collective expression of national pride as the crowd joined in a choir-like rendition of the song that many have come to regard as Jamaica’s unofficial second anthem.

Earlier in the evening, fellow honoree Wayne Wonder delivered a short but memorable set that traced the soundtrack of his decades-long career. Hits including No Letting Go, Saddest Day, I Don’t Know Why, Joyride, and Informer reverberated throughout the stadium, proving exactly why he too was deserving of the night’s Reggae Icon Award.

With each song Wayne Wonder showcased a musical legacy that has transcended generations, one that continues to bridge the gap between Jamaica’s past and present.

The evening’s nostalgia extended far beyond the honorees. A spirited Festival song sound clash featuring DJ Oliver and DJ Rasarella sent patrons on a journey through time as classics such as B am Bam, Baba Boom, Sweet and Dandy, Chiquitita, and Land of My Birth filled the space.

The celebration of Jamaica’s musical heritage continued when Roy Rayon took to the stage with his 1987 Festival Song winner, Thanks and Praises. The familiar melody had patrons clapping and singing along, signalling that the festivities for year 64 were in fully swing.

Then came the gospel segment, a fitting reminder that faith remains woven into the fabric of Jamaican identity.

Kevin Downswell captivated the audience with spirited renditions of You Make Me Stronger, Carry Me, and If It’s Not You, delivering a performance that balanced reverence with infectious energy.

Sebastian Braham followed with his beloved Hard Road to Travel medley, breathing new life into timeless favourites, including I Am Determined, Some Sweet Day, I Know Where I’m Going, and I Am Under the Rock.

Sister Pat transformed the stadium into a revival ground, leading patrons through classics such as Massa God A God, The Lord Is My Shepherd, and Come By Here, Lord. As thousands danced and sang along, her call for Jamaicans to give thanks for 64 years of nationhood was met with thunderous applause.

The programme also paid homage to Jamaica’s cultural roots with a breathtaking dance presentation,

Ode to Africa, and a musical showcase titled Celebrating Kingston: The Creative City of Music, which highlighted the genres born on Jamaican soil — mento, ska, rocksteady, reggae, and dancehall. This segment saw performances from dBURNZ, Janeen Mills, Noel Ellis, and reggae icon Marcia Griffiths.

Yet perhaps the night’s most moving moment came during the annual drone show. Already a crowd favourite, this year’s spectacle carried an emotional weight that transcended entertainment. Against the darkness of the night sky, 1,000 drones recreated not only the symbols synonymous with Jamaican culture, but also the destructive path carved by Hurricane Melissa in October 2025.

What unfolded was not simply a retelling of devastation but a testament to survival. As stories of communities rebuilding and neighbours supporting neighbours accompanied the display, the narrative shifted from loss to resilience. Praying hands illuminated the night sky as Chris Malachi’s Brighter Day echoed throughout the stadium. In that moment, Jamaica’s greatest strength became unmistakably clear — its people, their faith and unwavering determination to rise. Vibrant firework displays brought the curtains down on another Grand Gala celebration in recognition of 64 years of Independence and resilience of the Jamaican spirit.

World.title: US court orders halt to Trump ballroom construction
World.content:
A view of the ongoing construction of a helipad (left) and ballroom (right) at the White House, as seen from the Washington Monument observation deck in Washington, DC on July 23, 2026.Photo: AFP

WASHINGTON, United States (AFP) — An appeals court on Friday upheld an order halting work on Donald Trump’s prized White House ballroom, setting up another battle in the Supreme Court over the limits of presidential authority.

The US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit, which had allowed construction to continue while it considered the case, agreed with a lower court that such a massive White House overhaul required the explicit consent of Congress.

It stayed its own decision for two weeks to give Trump time to ask the Supreme Court to intervene.

The Republican president lashed out after the 2-1 ruling, calling it “horrendous, politically motivated, and unlawful”.

The two judges in the majority were appointed by Democratic presidents, while the dissenter was nominated by Trump himself.

The president vowed in a lengthy social media post to immediately appeal to the Supreme Court, while reiterating his argument that the entire project represented a matter of national security.

Trump initially touted the construction of the ballroom as being necessary to host galas, but has since repeatedly pointed to the concurrent addition of an underground military bunker and other security features.

Under the district judge’s initial order, work was to be allowed to continue only on a limited set of structures, including those that were underground.

“This holding has nothing at all to do with whether the proposed ballroom is desirable, or not, as a matter of policy. This ruling does not even necessarily mean that the defendants may not ultimately construct the ballroom,” the majority wrote Friday.

“What it does mean is that the defendants may not do so during the district court’s expeditious litigation without securing congress’s authorisation, as the Constitution and laws require.”

Trump, who has repeatedly complained that the White House lacks sufficient space for grand galas such as state dinners, unilaterally ordered construction of the massive ballroom.

Work on the project began last year with the sudden demolition of the White House’s entire historic East Wing.

Since then, photos have shown significant work on a basement complex, with some concrete walls rising up above ground.

Trump has insisted that the ballroom will be privately financed, but media reports in June showed that significant taxpayer funds were going to the project, which could cost as much as US$600 million.

While the White House initially cited a US$200-million price tag for the project, it quickly doubled the estimate to US$400 million.

The ballroom is just one of Trump’s pet projects to leave his mark on Washington by the time he leaves office in 2029, along with a renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other parks, as well as the construction of a gigantic arch.

Several of the projects have similarly faced legal challenges, but the ballroom project would be the first to reach the Supreme Court.

World.title: Three alleged exotic dancers from Dom Rep charged with work permit breaches
World.content:
MONTEGO BAY, St James — Three women from the Dominican Republic and two Jamaican nightclub owners appeared in the St James Parish Court on Wednesday facing charges of working without a permit and aiding and abetting that offence.

Marsol Beaz Beaz, Yahaira Jimena Tejeda Sanchez and Naiomi Perez, of the Dominican Republic, appeared alongside Jamaicans Camoy Spence and Nicholas Ricketts before Parish Judge Diahann Bernard.

All five are represented by attorney-at-law Adrian Dayes.

The allegations stem from an operation conducted on August 3 by members of the St James Police Division and the Trafficking in Persons Unit at a nightclub on Barnett Street, Montego Bay, St James, following information about suspected human trafficking activities at the establishment.

According to the prosecution, the cops saw the three Dominican women with several Jamaican exotic dancers at the nightclub.

The women were interviewed and subsequently arrested and charged with working without a permit, while the nightclub owners were charged with aiding and abetting working without a permit.

During the hearing, Dayes told the court that his clients were lawfully in Jamaica and were not working at the time of the operation.

A translator from the Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency assisted with the proceedings but Dayes told the court that the defence was still taking instructions and preferred to use its own translator rather than relying on the State.

The clerk of court clerk indicated that the three women have permission to remain in Jamaica until September 2 and indicated that the prosecution anticipates calling additional witnesses.

The clerk further indicated that the surety who previously secured bail for the three women advised that the arrangement only covered Wednesday’s court appearance.

Bernard subsequently granted the three women bail in the sum of $100,000 each, in their own surety, and ordered them to surrender their travel documents.

The matter was adjourned to September 2 for case management. Bail for Spence and Ricketts was extended.

World.title: More to come
World.content:
Jamaica’s Shanoya Douglas (left) and American Mia Maxwell (centre) both lunge for the finish line in the women’s 100m final at the World Under-20 Championships on Thursday at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon. Maxwell won in 11.14 seconds, just ahead of Douglas, 11.17. At right, Italy’s Kelly Ann Edimo finished third to take the bronze medal in 11.27. Paul Reid

OREGON, USA — Shanoya Douglas says her quest for an individual gold medal at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships is not over, as she gets ready for her preferred 200m after taking the silver in the 100m on Thursday.

Douglas and Gary Card, who came into the championships as world leaders in the 100m, were beaten into second-place finishes by Americans Mia Maxwell and Tate Taylor, respectively. It was only the second time athletes from the same country had won both gold medals in the 100m at the same Under-20 Championships, after Noah Lyles and Candace Hill won in 2016 in Bydgoszcz, Poland.

These were the first medals for Jamaica at the championships.

Both Douglas and Card had advanced to their respective 200m semi-finals after qualifying in the first round on Friday’s morning session.

Douglas, who also leads the women’s 200m ranking, says she was happy with her silver medal — her second individual medal at the World Under-20s — after winning bronze in the 200m two years ago in Lima, Peru. She, however, underlined that she is still hungry for more.

“The championships are not over yet. I still have the 200m, and there is still room to correct and to get my mental space where it is supposed to be — and it is not easy to win all the time,” she said. “I am not going to lay down and take silver; I am coming back stronger and better in the 200m.”

Douglas, who broke the national junior record twice this year, has a best of 22.11 seconds, and tied for third-best all-time with American legend Allyson Felix, says she knows what to fix.

“There are some tweaks and twerks to getting me where I’m at, and it’s on a bigger stage where anything is possible. It is just to come out on the day and perform. I felt like [Mia] came out on the day, and that’s it. She got the edge over me this time [but] it’s not gonna be the last. We’ll see each again on a different stage where we run together, and I feel like I’ll be winning too.”

Card was grateful for his medal. And after placing sixth two years ago in Lima, Peru, he said things could have been different and he was grateful.

“I know I could have done better but, just to be honest, just to be in the moment right here, healthy, being able to do what I did, it could have gone so many other ways, could have gone much worse but I’m just glad that God allowed me to finish healthy and came home with this medal. So, I’m grateful,” Card said.

“It’s very good that I’m one of the best under-20 athletes right now. We’re all going to be seniors soon — and all seniors also came through the junior ranks — and there is not a lot of generations [of athletes] who have performed like how we perform out here so everybody should be grateful. I feel like everybody should be grateful, and everybody should just be happy about it,” added Card.

He had high praises for Taylor, who he said was an “amazing person … So I’m very glad for him, and I was honoured to be sort of seen to be his rival in this event. I am grateful, I know he’s grateful, so I’m just glad it both worked out well, in some way, for both of us.”

Card got off to a fast start but was chased and caught by Taylor who passed him to win in a personal best 9.94 seconds (0.1m/s). The Jamaican was second in 10.05 seconds, and South Africa’s Marko Ferreira took the bronze with 10.16 seconds.

Maxwell got the edge over Douglas at the start and held off the Jamaican to the tape, running 11.14 seconds (-0.1m/s), Douglas ran 11.17 seconds, with Italy’s Kelly Ann Maevane Doualla Edimo taking the bronze medal with 11.27 seconds.

Theianna-Lee Terrelonge was sixth in 11.37 seconds

Maxwell’s win was the first time in 10 years that an American took the women’s 100m and snapped the run by Jamaicans, who won the last four editions – Briana Williams in 2018, Tina Clayton in 2021 and 2022 and Alana Reid in 2024.

World.title: 92 NCU graduands initiated into nursing profession
World.content:
Sudane Spence (left) receives the top student awards for both the theoretical and clinical aspects of the four-year nursing degree programme at NCU during the Nurses’ Pinning and Thanksgiving Ceremony held August 5. She celebrates the moment with NCU Interim President Dr Vivienne Quarrie (centre) and keynote speaker Dr Nicola Brown, director of nursing services at the National Chest Hospital.

THE latest batch of nurses trained by Northern Caribbean University (NCU) was welcomed into the profession by Dr Nicola Brown, director of nursing services at the National Chest Hospital, who delivered the keynote address during the Nurses’ Pinning and Thanksgiving Service held on August 5 at the Mandeville-based institution.

The pinning ceremony marked the completion of four years of classroom instruction and clinical experience in the field by the nursing students.

Several practicing nurses participated in affixing pins to the graduands symbolising their initiation into the profession.

Dr Brown pointed out to the graduands that the pin represents a solemn covenant of service and responsibility and is a visible reminder that they are entering a profession “where knowledge meets humanity and skill meets compassion”.

Speaking on the theme ‘Transformed Minds, Compassionate Hearts for Christ-centred Service,’ Dr Brown highlighted several situations that the new nurses will face in delivering care.

She pointed out that these could include patients with “more complex health problems” which increasingly require mental health services and underscored that the new nurses will require the required knowledge, wisdom and situational awareness to provide appropriate patient care.

While noting the benefits of technology in delivering health care, Dr Brown warned against it becoming a barrier between the nurse and the “human being in the bed”.

The health administrator also advised the graduands to resist peer pressure in a working environment that tests their morale and professional ethics.

She argued that a transformed mind resists cynicism and refuses to become desensitised to the suffering of others, but instead recognises each patient as a person of inherent dignity, worthy of respect and compassionate care.

“Compassion bridges the gap between clinical competence and genuine care, making patients seen and valued,” said Dr Brown.

Turning to the prospect of burnout caused by nursing shortage and high turnover rates amid systemic pressures, Dr Brown advised the nurse graduands that in such moments it is their compassion that will sustain their calling.

She pointed to a link between compassion and Christ-centred service which is to embody love in action, demonstrating patience, kindness, humility, and grace in every interaction.

“Christ-centered service also requires integrity and courage in the face of challenges within health-care systems. It calls you to do what is right, even when no one is watching, and to advocate for those who cannot advocate for themselves,” added Dr Brown.

In her remarks to graduands, NCU Interim President Dr Vivienne Quarrie said nurses from the institution are recognised across Jamaica and the international community for their creativity, competence, and character.

She said their training was intentionally designed to transform their minds and shape compassionate hearts for service that reflects Christ-centred qualities.

“So, as you are pinned today, may you always remember that you were prepared to provide ethical service and to serve with unwavering moral commitment. Accordingly, may your transformed minds and compassionate hearts guide your practice, inspire your patients, and honour the one true God who has taken you to this point,” said Dr Quarrie.

Graduand Sudane Spence received the top student awards for both the theoretical and clinical aspects of the nursing degree programme.

Spence said she is eagerly looking forward to changing the lives of patients for the better using the knowledge and skills she and her fellow students gained over the four years of training at NCU.

The nurse graduands will participate in the NCU 103rd Commencement Ceremony to be held on Sunday.

World.title: Magyar’s party backs former supreme court head for Hungarian president
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s ruling Tisza party said on Saturday that it had nominated former Supreme Court President András Baka to become the country’s next president.

Baka, who worked as a judge on the European Court of Human Rights before being elected to head the Supreme Court, was removed from his post by the Fidesz government in 2011 — a move the ECHR ruled was unlawful.

“Throughout his career, Dr. András Baka has considered the principle of the separation of powers to be of paramount importance and has consistently stood up for the rule of law and judicial independence,” Tisza said in a Facebook post.

World.title: Sánchez-Meloni clash brings back borders — and headaches for tourists
World.content:
Madrid has pushed back forcefully against that narrative, and noted that the migrants could not leave the North African territory because they lack valid IDs required to travel on ferries to mainland Europe.

Spanish authorities and the European Commission this week confirmed that none of the 72,000 people who surged into Ceuta have crossed the Strait of Gibraltar. During a meeting of EU interior ministers on Tuesday, Italian Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi publicly praised Spain for its handling of the situation and expressed Rome’s “sincere solidarity” with Madrid.

Yet despite requests from Madrid, the Italian government has declined to end border checks even after it became clear that there was no risk of the Ceuta crisis spilling into the rest of Europe. Rome’s inaction prompted Spain to issue a statement on Friday threatening to adopt “proportional measures” if Rome did not change course by Aug. 9.

After Meloni’s office responded by declaring “Italy does not accept ultimatums or demands from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Madrid moved to reintroduce its own controls.

Magnus Brunner, the European commissioner for internal affairs and migration, sought to mediate in the dispute.

“I was in contact with both the Spanish and Italian Interior Ministers today. Both confirmed that the internal border controls are temporary,” Brunner said in a post on X. “I stressed the progress we’ve made on tackling illegal migration and that trust between Member States is our most valuable currency.”

World.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 12, wound over 80 overnight
World.content:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the drone attacks killed three people — a 3-year-old child and the child’s grandparents — in a village in the Kyiv region. The six ballistic missiles struck civilian infrastructure in Kyiv, killing one person, he said.

“More pressure is needed. New sanctions that will prevent the production of these ballistic missiles,” Zelenskyy said on X. “And we definitely need more protection for our people,” he added, appealing to allies to provide missile interceptors to strengthen Ukraine’s defenses against Russia’s aerial assault.

In the Zaporizhzhia region, in southeast Ukraine, three people were killed and four were wounded following the overnight attack, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said.

A further five people were killed and nearly 50 people wounded in the regions of Kharkiv, Donetsk and Kherson, according to regional authorities.

Separately, Zelenskyy visited Serbia on Saturday — his first trip to the country since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine — to meet with President Aleksandar Vučić and Prime Minister Đuro Macut.

Zelenskyy said the talks had focused on rebuilding infrastructure, readying a free-trade agreement this year, and preparing for the winter to come.

World.title: Gabriel Attal alleges Russian interference in French presidential race
World.content:
Gabriel Attal attends a session of questions to the government at the National Assembly, in Paris on January 6, 2026. | Christophe Petit Tesson/EPA

Attal becomes the latest contender to file a complaint over alleged Russian interference ahead of the April 2027 presidential vote.

Former prime minister and presidential candidate Gabriel Attal has filed a complaint over an alleged Russian disinformation campaign ahead of next year’s French presidential election, local news outlets reported on Saturday.

Attal’s lawyers told French media that the complaint, filed on Friday, denounces “acts of foreign interference, manipulation of information, fabrication of content likely to undermine the fundamental interests of the nation and the sincerity of the upcoming presidential election.”

They told BFMTV that several accounts on social network X, some of which impersonated French and international media, had disseminated fake video reports and newspaper articles attributing false statements to Attal that were “intended to discredit him as a candidate.”
