World.title: Canadian Estonian family still thriving 30 years after return to homeland
World.content:
The Viinalass family recently celebrated 30 years in Estonia, reflecting on how a temporary move to their homeland became permanent, coming full circle after generations.

The family marked the milestone with a gathering of about 150 relatives and friends, who shared memories from their early years after moving from Canada.

"Our mom was in charge of the Facebook event," recalled Joshua James Viinalass, a real estate broker with Arco Vara.

"She accidentally sent the invite to everyone," added his brother, musician Daniel Levi. "And everyone responded that they're coming."

Like in many diaspora Estonian families, the Viinalass brothers' grandfather was a World War II-era refugee, who first fled to Germany in 1944 before reaching and later naturalizing as a citizen in Canada.

Their father, Linden Viinalass, was born and raised in Canada, where his children were also born and spent the first few years of their lives. After their grandfather's death in the 1990s, however, their father came across an ad in a Canadian Estonian diaspora newspaper seeking English teachers in Estonia.

"He immediately knew that [opportunity] was meant for him — like it spoke to him almost supernaturally," Daniel Levi said.

The plan was simple: move to Estonia for a year and then return to Canada. Thirty years later, the family is still here and thriving.

Adjusting as kids

Joshua James and Daniel Levi were just 3 and 8 years old when their family moved to Tartu, and some of their earliest memories are of life in and around the Soviet-era prefab apartment buildings in Annelinn.

Viinalass family photos. Source: Viinalass family/ERR

Joshua James said he picked up Estonian simply playing with other kids on the playground and in kindergarten.

Daniel Levi recalled his father giving a neighbor's child a soccer ball, which prompted an unexpected gift to the Viinalass family in turn.

"The family was so touched that they gifted us a drinking horn brought all the way from Georgia in return," he said, adding that the horn is still proudly displayed at their parents' home.

The musician acknowledged that the move from Canada to Estonia took some getting used to for all of them, but added that the younger you are, the easier it can be to adjust.

"Speaking of adjusting, just today I was talking to someone about what our favorite parts of kindergarten had been," said Joshua James. "I remember I couldn't understand a word at first, but when meals were served, that was the best part of the day."

Both brothers praised Estonian food, agreeing that one of their favorite Estonian dishes is still hakklihakaste — a simple creamed ground meat often served with potatoes and popular both in Estonia and the diaspora.

Years after a previous appearance on ETV's "Ringvaade," however, Daniel Levi admitted he still can't bring himself to eat sült, or meat aspic.

Brothers Daniel Levi Viinalass and James Joshua Viinalass. August 2026. Source: ERR

'Three men sitting in a sauna'

Asked whether Estonia lives up to its digital image, the Viiinalass brothers pointed out that the contrast is evident when they talk to friends in the U.S. who still have to deposit physical paychecks in person at the bank, or grapple with filing tax returns that in Estonia take literally just a few clicks to do.

They also agreed Estonians seem to be warming up to things like hugging, although the perception that Estonians are typically reserved and need their personal space persists.

"Estonians like their fresh air and pure nature, and I think that sense of personal space goes beyond just that question of hugging," said Daniel Levi.

"I think it's very healthy," Joshua James countered, prompting his brother to quip that it's clear he was raised in Estonia. "That little bit of personal space is really welcome sometimes."

The real estate broker described his post-workout sauna at the gym earlier that day, calling it a perfectly Estonian example.

"Three men sitting in a sauna: no one says a word, no one makes eye contact, no one says 'Tere,' nothing," Joshua James said. "No, when I handed the water bucket over to one of the other guys in the sauna, he said, 'Aitäh.'"

World.title: Iraq oil exports drop 75% amid Hormuz closure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Oil Minister Hayan Abdul-Ghani announced on Saturday, August 8, 2026, that the nation’s crude oil exports have plummeted by 75% due to the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz and regional military escalations. The severe drop in oil revenues has triggered a liquidity squeeze across the federal government, causing widespread delays in state employee salary disbursements.

Speaking at a press conference in Baghdad, Abdul-Ghani revealed that Iraq is currently exporting only a quarter of its pre-war volumes, which stood at approximately 3.5 million barrels per day (bpd) prior to the outbreak of regional hostilities on February 28. He noted that while Baghdad has engaged in diplomatic talks with Iran to permit the passage of Iraqi oil shipments through the Gulf, no operational agreement has been activated.

Key financial and operational highlights

Export Collapse: Iraq’s crude exports have fallen to ~25% of pre-war capacity, cutting off the primary source of state revenue.

Fiscal Pressure & Salary Delays: Reduced export volumes and below-budget sale prices have caused acute liquidity shortages, delaying public sector payrolls.

Corporate Damage Compensation: Domestic Attacks: Baghdad has agreed to compensate foreign energy companies for damages resulting from attacks originating inside Iraqi territory. External Strikes: The government declared itself legally exempt from compensating firms for damages caused by foreign strikes or broader military actions beyond state control.

Alternative Export Bypasses: Baghdad is fast-tracking pipeline infrastructure projects bypassing the Persian Gulf, including routes south toward Turkey’s Ceyhan port, Syria’s Baniyas terminal, and Jordan’s Aqaba port.

To maintain minimal cash flows, Iraq is currently forced to sell its crude at deep price concessions below the baseline benchmark set in the national budget, compounding treasury deficits.

In response to the prolonged maritime chokehold in the Strait of Hormuz, the Ministry of Oil is accelerating infrastructure development along overland export routes.

Priority has been placed on expanding and constructing pipeline corridors connecting southern production hubs to the Mediterranean via Syria and Turkey, alongside long-term transit planning toward the Red Sea via Jordan.

World.title: Iraq activates Kirkuk oil field development contract with BP
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Saturday, August 8, 2026, the official activation of its Kirkuk oilfield development contract with British energy giant BP. The project aims to elevate crude oil production from its current capacity of 320,000 barrels per day (bpd) to a peak target of 420,000 bpd.

Ministry of Oil Spokesperson Salim Al-Rikabi stated that the contract—initially signed in September 2025—focuses on expanding crude extraction while capturing associated natural gas to eliminate routine flaring and feed domestic power generation infrastructure.

Key operational targets & metrics

Crude Oil Output: Increasing current production from 320,000 bpd to a peak target of 420,000 bpd.

Associated Gas Capture: Raising associated gas processing from 255 million standard cubic feet per day (scf/d) to a peak capacity of 400 million scf/d.

Facility Modernization: Upgrading and expanding infrastructure across North Oil Company fields and North Gas Company processing plants.

Power & Social Infrastructure: Constructing a dedicated 400-megawatt (MW) power plant, expanding local employment, funding community development initiatives, and upskilling North Oil and North Gas workforces.

Environmental Impact: Phasing out continuous gas flaring to redirect captured methane directly into national electricity generation.

The activation of the Kirkuk project represents a major component of Iraq’s broader energy strategy to achieve natural gas self-sufficiency and reduce reliance on imported fuel.

By upgrading processing facilities managed by the North Gas Company and constructing a dedicated 400 MW power generation facility, the initiative directly addresses regional electricity shortages while reducing environmental emissions.

The partnership also reinforces BP’s operational footprint in northern Iraq, complementing its long-standing management of the Southern Rumaila field and bolstering state-led efforts to modernize national energy infrastructure.

World.title: India’s Reliance pays record $25 million freight cost for Iraqi crude amid Hormuz crisis
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — India’s Reliance Industries (RELI.NS), operator of the world’s largest refining complex in Gujarat, paid an unprecedented record charter fee of $23 million to $25 million for a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) to transport 2 million barrels of Basrah crude from Iraq, according to shipping sources cited by Reuters on Friday, August 7, 2026.

The extreme freight surge—marking a jump from a pre-war average of $2 million to 12 times the baseline global freight rate—highlights severe shipping chokepoints in the Strait of Hormuz caused by the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict. Daily vessel transits through the strategic waterway have plummeted from a pre-war average of 125–140 ships to a fraction of normal capacity as shipowners avoid military risks.

Key financial & logistics metrics

Soaring Freight Rates: Reliance chartered the VLCC from South Korea’s Sinokor at 1,200 points on the Worldscale freight index—12 times the reference benchmark—up from pre-war levels of 0.8 to 0.9 times ($2 million total).

Deep SOMO Discounts: To offset soaring shipping costs and attract buyers into the Gulf, the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) offered steep discounts of $25 to $30 per barrel below Dubai regional benchmarks.

Net Margin Offset: Despite the $25 million freight tag, energy analysts estimate Reliance will still save millions on the overall transaction due to Iraq’s heavy crude price reductions.

Limited Carrier Pool: Sinokor remains one of the few international maritime operators willing to navigate the Strait of Hormuz to load cargo at Iraq’s Basra Oil Terminal.

While Asian refiners—particularly across India and China—are actively seeking chartered tankers to capture Iraq’s discounted crude allocations, shipowner reluctance continues to limit available tonnage entering the Gulf.

By offering deep price concessions, Iraq’s oil marketing arm is successfully maintaining crude flow off the Basra coast despite soaring war-risk insurance premiums and maritime transport bottlenecks.

World.title: Kata’ib Sayyid Al Shuhada clarifies delay in retaliatory strikes against U.S.-Saudi targets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Abu Ala al-Walai, Secretary-General of Kata’ib Sayyid al-Shuhada, commented on Saturday, August 8, 2026, regarding the decision by the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” to pause planned military responses to recent joint U.S.-Saudi strikes.

Speaking via a statement on social media platform X, al-Walai confirmed that the delay was granted at the direct request of Coordination Framework leaders, led by Badr Organization chief Hadi al-Amiri, alongside several independent political figures. However, the paramilitary commander emphasized that options for retaliation—including the reassessment of its timing, scale, and nature—remain fully on the table. He urged state officials to utilize this temporary window to secure Iraq’s rights through diplomatic and legal channels.

Key developments in the escalation pause

The Deferred Response: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq announced on Friday, August 7, the postponement of retaliatory operations originally scheduled for the 23rd of Safar targeting Saudi Arabia and U.S. military bases.

Al-Amiri’s Appeal: Badr Organization leader Hadi al-Amiri issued an urgent video address early Friday urging armed factions to delay military action following American-Saudi strikes on Iraqi territory, prioritizing national stability while pursuing accountability for casualties via diplomatic means.

High Security Readiness: The political appeal followed a volatile night across Baghdad and multiple governorates, prompting high-level security alerts and military deployments across the capital.

Command Structure On Site: In response to directives from Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi to elevate combat readiness, senior commanders from Baghdad Operations Command were deployed on the ground to enforce military discipline and secure vital sectors.

The brief pause in military operations provides a critical window for Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s administration to manage state security, navigate delicate diplomatic channels with Washington and Riyadh, and prevent further regional escalation.

World.title: Iraq fish deaths: 7 alarming signs of a deepening water and pollution crisis
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Recurring Iraq fish deaths are becoming an increasingly serious environmental and economic warning, with the Green Iraq Observatory describing the phenomenon as an annual pattern that reflects the accumulation of two interconnected crises: worsening water scarcity and persistent pollution.

Rather than representing isolated incidents caused by temporary changes in river conditions, the repeated deaths of large numbers of fish across Iraq’s rivers, canals and marshlands suggest that the country’s aquatic ecosystems are coming under sustained pressure from declining water flows, untreated wastewater, industrial pollution and weaknesses in water management.

The latest incidents, recorded in April and August 2026, have once again raised concerns about the condition of Iraq’s freshwater resources and the government’s ability to protect them. According to the observatory, more than 1,000 tonnes of fish died in the Tigris and Diyala rivers during April, with particularly heavy losses reported in Wasit province, while a separate incident occurred earlier this month in the Al-Amshan Canal in Maysan.

Although the two incidents were associated with different immediate circumstances, they demonstrate how vulnerable Iraq’s aquatic ecosystems have become when declining water levels interact with pollution and inadequate environmental controls.

Iraq fish deaths are becoming an annual warning sign

The Green Iraq Observatory argues that the recurrence of mass fish deaths should no longer be treated as a series of unrelated environmental emergencies. According to its assessment, similar incidents have occurred repeatedly across different parts of Iraq over the past several years, yet the underlying causes have not been addressed with sufficient consistency to prevent them from returning.

This pattern is particularly concerning because rivers and wetlands are not only ecological assets; they also support fisheries, agriculture and the livelihoods of communities that depend directly on healthy waterways.

The observatory said the April incident involved more than 1,000 tonnes of dead fish in the Tigris and Diyala rivers, with the largest losses concentrated in Wasit. It attributed the event to severe contamination caused by untreated sewage and industrial waste, while also pointing to increased water releases from Hamrin Dam that reportedly moved accumulated pollutants downstream toward the Tigris.

The organization further said that more than 20 people experienced poisoning or skin-related injuries and were taken to hospital, illustrating how deterioration in water quality can potentially extend beyond damage to aquatic life and become a broader public-health concern.

A second incident was reported at the beginning of August in the Al-Amshan Canal in Maysan. According to the observatory, the agriculture and water committee of the Maysan Provincial Council attributed the fish deaths to a sharp decline in the water releases allocated to the canal.

This episode is significant because it demonstrates that pollution is not necessarily the only immediate trigger for fish mortality; inadequate water flows can also create conditions in which fish become increasingly vulnerable to high temperatures, reduced oxygen levels and the concentration of pollutants already present in the water.

Water scarcity Is only part of the problem

Iraq’s water crisis is frequently discussed in terms of declining river flows, prolonged drought and reductions in water arriving from upstream countries. Those factors are undoubtedly important, but the recent fish deaths suggest that the country’s environmental problems cannot be explained simply by saying that Iraq does not have enough water. The quality, distribution and management of the water available can be just as important as its overall volume.

The Green Iraq Observatory highlighted this distinction by noting that the country’s total water storage had reportedly risen to around 34 billion cubic meters at the time of the latest incident.

From the organization’s perspective, the fact that fish mortality continued despite an increase in total reserves indicates that administrative decisions concerning water distribution may be contributing to the problem alongside genuine resource scarcity.

This does not mean that Iraq’s wider water shortage is unimportant. On the contrary, prolonged drought and declining inflows can weaken the natural ability of rivers and wetlands to dilute pollutants and maintain ecological balance. However, when available water is distributed unevenly or when polluted water is allowed to enter already stressed waterways, the consequences can become significantly more severe.

In other words, the crisis is not simply about how much water Iraq has, but also about where the water goes, what quality it has and how effectively it is managed.

Pollution can turn a water shortage into an ecological emergency

Untreated sewage and industrial waste are among the most serious threats facing Iraq’s waterways because they can fundamentally alter the chemical and biological conditions required for aquatic life. When large quantities of organic material enter a river or canal, microorganisms consume oxygen while breaking that material down, potentially reducing dissolved oxygen to levels that fish and other aquatic organisms cannot tolerate.

The situation can become even more complicated when water temperatures rise or when algae proliferate excessively. Some forms of harmful algae can contribute to oxygen depletion, particularly when large quantities of organic matter subsequently decompose.

At the same time, reduced water flows can prevent pollutants from being dispersed naturally, leaving them concentrated in particular sections of a river, canal or wetland.

This combination of factors helps explain why pollution and water scarcity should not be treated as completely separate problems. A waterway with strong flows may have a greater capacity to dilute certain pollutants, whereas a shallow and poorly circulated waterway can become significantly more vulnerable to contamination.

Consequently, environmental protection requires both adequate water releases and strict control over what is discharged into the country’s rivers.

Iraq has experienced similar fish mortality events for years

The latest incidents are not without precedent. The Green Iraq Observatory cited a long record of mass fish mortality events in Iraq, including a major incident in the Euphrates in Babylon in 2018, when tens of thousands of tonnes of fish were reportedly affected.

This was followed by the death of millions of fish at the Hindiya Barrage and another major incident in Al-Dalm Marsh in Diwaniyah in 2020.

Further incidents were reported in the Al-Ezz River in Maysan in 2023, while extensive fish deaths occurred in Ibn Najm Marsh in Najaf last year. Particularly worrying is the recurrence of fish mortality in the Maysan area where a similar incident had already been recorded, because repeated events in the same geographic location can indicate that the environmental conditions responsible for the original problem have not been adequately corrected.

The observatory argues that the repeated nature of these incidents is difficult to reconcile with a system that relies primarily on temporary investigative committees after environmental damage has already occurred. Investigations can establish causes and responsibility, but they cannot substitute for permanent monitoring mechanisms capable of identifying dangerous changes in water quality before they result in large-scale ecological losses.

Iraq’s Marshlands face particular risks

The Iraqi marshlands are especially sensitive to changes in water availability and quality because their ecological health depends on a delicate relationship between water flows, seasonal conditions and the surrounding environment. These wetlands provide habitat for fish and birds while supporting communities whose economic and cultural lives have developed around them over generations.

When water levels fall sharply, sections of the marshes can become isolated or excessively shallow, increasing temperatures and reducing oxygen circulation. If polluted water enters these already stressed environments, the damage can become significantly more difficult to reverse.

Protecting Iraq’s marshlands therefore requires a long-term approach that connects water policy with environmental policy. Maintaining adequate ecological flows, reducing pollution and establishing continuous monitoring systems would be far more effective than treating each fish mortality event as an isolated emergency.

What Iraq can do to prevent future fish deaths

The Green Iraq Observatory has called for several measures aimed at addressing the structural causes behind recurring fish mortality. Among its recommendations is the establishment of fair and sustainable water allocations for provinces and marshlands, rather than relying on short-term decisions that may leave some waterways dangerously depleted.

The observatory has also called for stronger environmental oversight of wastewater treatment facilities and industrial establishments located near rivers. Effective enforcement would require more than regulations on paper; authorities would need regular inspections, reliable water-quality testing and meaningful consequences for facilities that discharge untreated or inadequately treated waste.

Another important proposal is the creation of an early-warning system that monitors dissolved oxygen and pollution levels. Such a system could bring together government agencies, universities and civil-society organizations, allowing scientific data to be collected continuously and shared quickly when dangerous changes are detected.

Finally, rapid compensation for fish farmers affected by major environmental incidents could provide essential economic relief while investigations determine responsibility and long-term solutions.

No. Water scarcity is an important contributing factor, but pollution and poor water management can also play major roles. Even when overall water reserves increase, individual rivers, canals or marshes may experience insufficient flows or deteriorating water quality.

World.title: US Fed sends $500 million cash shipment to Iraq amid financial pressures
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The United States Federal Reserve has sent a new $500 million cash cargo to the Central Bank of Iraq, providing additional dollar liquidity as Baghdad grapples with rising financial pressures and disruptions to its oil-dependent economy.

The shipment was announced by Iraq’s national news agency, citing an official source who claimed the dollars will be used for permitted overseas transfers and transactions involving Iraqi citizens.

Further supplies are planned each month, with a government official estimating annual cash delivery of $8 billion to $10 billion.

These cash payments are part of Iraq’s peculiar financial relationship with the United States.

Proceeds from Iraqi oil exports are mostly placed in an account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, with Baghdad obtaining dollars via permitted transfers and cash shipments administered by the Central Bank of Iraq.

The new supply comes at a critical moment for Iraq’s budget.

The disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has increased pressure on a nation that relies significantly on oil exports to support government expenditures and get foreign currency.

Iraq’s enormous public-sector pay bill contributes to this vulnerability.

Millions of Iraqis rely directly or indirectly on government wages, pensions, and social benefits; therefore, stable oil income and liquidity are crucial to the national budget.

Baghdad has lately expressed increased worries about its capacity to fulfill expenditure obligations if oil earnings continue low, strengthening long-standing demands for Iraq to diversify government income and lessen its reliance on petroleum exports.

The most recent dollar cargo should offer further liquidity to Iraq’s banking system, but it also shows the country’s vulnerability to both oil-market shocks and its financial ties with Washington at a time of rising regional tensions.

World.title: Lise Klaveness, the Norwegian thorn in Infantino’s side
World.content:
Oslo – A rare woman in the top echelons of football, the head of Norway’s federation Lise Klaveness has been a thorn in FIFA’s side for years.

Now, some would gladly see her take over the leadership of football’s international governing body from Gianni Infantino.

The 45-year-old lawyer and former footballer who played 73 matches for Norway has been highly vocal about international football’s woes under Infantino.

The Swiss-Italian has been mired in controversy since his plan to open FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors was swiftly rejected last week.

On Friday she called for him to resign.

When he was elected FIFA president in 2016, “he was a candidate who had been elected on a reform programme focused on good governance,” she told AFP.

“Then things quickly deteriorated: from keeping a distance, we moved to giving up, and even backtracking, all against a backdrop of a lack of independence from heads of state and other influential figures, particularly from World Cup host countries,” she said.

She fired her first salvo at Infantino in 2022, just after she was appointed head of the Norwegian federation, about the conditions under which the World Cup was awarded to Qatar.

From Doha, she publicly lamented that “human rights, equality, democracy, the core interests of football, were not in the starting 11”.

The following year, Norway refused to back Infantino in his re-election bid, signalling its dissatisfaction with his leadership.

Klaveness “was in a way the first standard-bearer for much of this criticism that many others now share when it comes to the way Infantino runs FIFA,” said Mina Finsted Berg, a sports commentator for Norwegian channel TV2.

She “is very committed to ensuring that rules and decisions are respected,” she added.

– Trump, Balogun and investors –

The reasons for her outrage against Infantino have piled up in recent months: FIFA’s decision to award a “Peace Prize” to US President Donald Trump, with whom Infantino has a conspicuously close relationship; the lifting of the suspension of US player Folarin Balogun at the 2026 World Cup following an intervention by Trump; and the aborted plan to open FIFA to private investors.

The Norwegian federation has decided to bring all three issues before the Ethics Committee of the world football governing body.

Klaveness’s voice carries all the more weight after Norway, long absent from major international tournaments, enjoyed a strong run in this year’s World Cup before being knocked out in the quarter-finals by England.

Internationally, commentators have praised her “strong moral compass” and consider her a serious candidate to replace Infantino if he were to step down.

He is standing for re-election for a fourth and final term next March and is currently the only declared candidate.

“She was the only one who always took a clear stand and did not go along with the mainstream. And at FIFA, the time is right for a woman to take the lead,” former FIFA head Sepp Blatter — himself disgraced after a corruption scandal — wrote on social network X.

– Ballot box obstacles –

Klaveness herself has insisted that the crisis in world football should not be reduced to a simple “Game of Thrones” power struggle and has instead called for a renewed focus on good governance.

“For us, it has never been a personal issue against Gianni Infantino,” she told AFP. “The problems go beyond the person of the president.”

And while she “has registered” that her name is being tossed around as a possible successor, she brushed aside questions about whether she was a candidate: “We’re not there yet.”

Many obstacles remain.

“In addition to being seen as extremely radical in many places, especially outside Europe, she is a woman. That is also likely to count against her in many regions of the world,” Mina Finsted Berg said.

Even within Europe’s governing body UEFA, which one could presume would be most favourable to her, Klaveness failed to win election to the Executive Committee in 2023.

She only joined in 2025, when she was the sole candidate for the seat reserved for women.

“If she already has such a hard time getting elected in Europe, how could she convince Africans and South Americans?” asked Erik Thorstvedt, a former goalkeeper for the Norwegian national team turned commentator.

World.title: Clinton compares Trump’s White House to former Iraqi dictator Saddam’s palaces
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Former US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton has compared President Donald Trump’s White House renovations to former Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein’s palaces, remembering her own travels to Baghdad after his ouster.

Clinton, speaking on journalist Kara Swisher’s podcast, compared Trump’s White House decor to meetings she attended in Saddam Hussein’s former palaces while serving as a US senator.

“They were quite reminiscent of what we are seeing in our own White House,” she said.

Her remarks come amid wider criticism of Trump’s renovations and architectural decisions, such as heavy gold décor within the Oval Office, plans for a new White House ballroom, and a projected triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

Clinton called the improvements “tacky” and suggested that the president was focusing too much on cosmetic initiatives when the US confronts substantial foreign policy, economic, and technological issues.

She also criticized the process around Trump’s planned ballroom, stating that she was not opposed to the White House having such a facility but was concerned about the architecture and how the project had been handled.

Given Clinton’s past with Iraq, the connection to Saddam was especially relevant.

She was a member of the United States Senate during the 2003 war that deposed Saddam Hussein and subsequently became Secretary of State under President Barack Obama.

During his reign, Saddam was noted for building multiple extravagant presidential palaces around Iraq, many with elaborate interiors and significant use of marble, chandeliers, and gold-colored décor, despite the country’s international sanctions and economic difficulty.

Trump has defended his White House restoration plans, which are part of a larger push to renovate and enhance Washington’s important federal buildings and sites.

Clinton’s parallel brings Iraq and one of Saddam’s most recognizable emblems into the increasingly heated political argument over Trump’s White House moves.

World.title: Gen Z is a force that can’t be ignored: Dharmendra Pradhan

World.title: EPFO, officers' body contest claims about new IT system
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Weeks after the rollout of the new centralised IT enabled system (CITES) early July by Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (

), which promised to enhance member convenience through faster automated claims settlements, field officials across the country have been "left to their own devices" to deal with the mounting claim pendencies as the new system faces strain, claimed the EPF Officers Association (EPFOA) in a letter to labour minister Mansukh Mandaviya.

Contrary to expectations that the majority of claims would be settled in 2-3 days, EPFOA claims that "lakhs of auto claims were kept pending in the system for more than 20 days, with no explanation to either the field offices or to the members."

However, EPFO has dismissed these and said this transition was implemented with minimal disruption of services, and the temporary increase in pendency was due to moving to a new enterprise-wide platform.

World.title: Captain moves crew to citadel, thwarts pirate assault on India-bound vessel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: On July 1, an attack by pirates on an India-bound bulk carrier, Golden Arsenal, in the Gulf of Aden was foiled after the captain moved all crew members, including an Indian seafarer, into the vesselâs âcitadelâ and sought assistance from the

.

A citadel is a fortified safe room with essential supplies such as food and water, as well as communication equipment, where crew members can take refuge during a pirate attack. The pirates failed to breach the citadel and eventually fled the vessel.

Sharing this incident at the National Port Security Conference this week, Captain Vikram Singh Manhas, deputy nautical adviser at DGMA (maritime regulator), urged all crew members and masters to remain vigilant and follow preventive measures prescribed under best management practices (BMP), amid a rise in piracy incidents.

Four vessels are held hostage by Somali pirates at present, three of which have Indian crew members aboard.

One of the vessels has one Indian seafarer, while the other two have five and 11 Indian crew, respectively.

Highlighting the significance of prevention in such cases, Manhas said that once a vessel is held by pirates, everything is dependent upon the negotiations with the pirates and that the government is working to ensure the safe release of Indian seafarers.

World.title: US Vice President JD Vance calls PM Modi to discuss boosting ties
World.content:

on Saturday as the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation in trade, defence, critical and emerging technologies, energy security and critical minerals.

World.title: Government appoints 30 judges to high courts of Calcutta, MP, Karnataka, Madras
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The law ministry notified the appointments of 30 judges for the high courts of Madras, Calcutta, Karnataka and MP on Saturday. The highest number of 15 judges have been appointed in the

World.title: Captain of turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight may have failed dope test
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The captain operating Air Indiaâs turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight on Tuesday (Aug 4) reportedly tested positive in a psychoactive substances (dope) test conducted on arrival, according to multiple sources.

The airline did not either confirm or deny it, saying while the tests were conducted, the results have not been shared with it.

âWe are aware that a post-flight screening test was conducted on the pilots in accordance with applicable protocols. However, the results of the test have not been shared with Air India, and we are therefore not in a position to comment on any findings,â an AI spokesperson said.

âAir India undertakes regular drug testing of crew members in compliance with civil aviation regulations, independent of any specific flight or operational incident.

We will continue to cooperate with the relevant authorities as required,â the airline added.

The Airbus A320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near Odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet. On arrival in Delhi, 13 passengers and four crew members were hospitalised. Sources say the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is probing this case from all angles including whether the handling of this turbulence event was correct; whether the event happened due to weather or some other reason; the likely impact on the aircraft like did it suffer hydraulic failure due to impact and whether it should have flown all the way to Delhi after the episode and not diverted to some nearby airport like Varanasi or Lucknow.





Pending probe, flight crew is taken off flying duty as per protocol. So the pilots of this flight are also not flying currently. DGCA rules stipulate that a pilot testing positive for consumption of psychoactive substances for the first time be referred to for de-addiction and rehabilitation. Such crew member can return for active duties with a negative dope test report.

World.title: Proposed MDR for UPI transactions will be nominal, says government
World.content:
Government officials have indicated that MDR of 0.25% to 0.4% may be allowed for UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, with a ceiling on the charge.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The government said on Saturday that the proposed merchant discount rate (MDR) for UPI transactions will be nominal and apply only to a limited set of merchants for transactions above a threshold, while seeking to assure users that all person-to-person transactions will remain free and consumers who make the payment will not face any fees."A vast majority of the transactions will remain free of charge for merchants on UPI. MDR, if introduced, will only be threshold-based and not levied on a blanket basis to all," the statement said, adding that the UPI and Services Steering Committee, headed by NPCI, will decide on the MDR, if any.It also dismissed reports of the charges being imposed under pressure from the US, which was seen to be pushing the case of Visa and Mastercard that levy MDR on credit card and debit card transactions, which are up to 2%, and usually not passed on to consumers unless the merchant is keen on a cash transaction. "If external pressure had been a factor, the government would not have introduced UPI in 2016 or made it free of charge for both merchants as well as citizens since Jan 2020 and ensured that it became the world's largest real-time interoperable payment system.The amendment should be viewed in the context of the government's broader objective of ensuring that India's digital payment infrastructure remains sustainable, competitive, and capable of serving the country's rapidly expanding digital economy."The finance ministry argued the move was necessary to expand the infrastructure into rural and semi-urban areas. Officials have indicated an MDR of 0.25% to 0.4% may be allowed for UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, provided they are not person-to-person, with a ceiling on the charge.

World.title: Government spending on education below Unesco's 15% standard
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India remains just above Unesco's minimum GDP benchmark for education, but the sector's share in government spending has slipped below the prescribed threshold. Education accounts for 4.1% of GDP but 14.2% of total public expenditure, down from 15.7% in 2015 and below the 15% benchmark, Unesco's 2026 SDG 4 scorecard has shown.

The funding picture assumes significance because India continues to lag on secondary school completion. Its latest lower secondary (Classes VI-VIII) completion rate is 86% as against its 99% national benchmark for 2025, while upper secondary (Classes IX-XII) completion rate is 51% as against 84%. Unesco classifies progress at both levels as slow.

Under the Education 2030 framework, countries committed to spending 4-6% of GDP and/or 15-20% of public expenditure on education.

The scorecard uses the lower thresholds as minimum benchmarks. India meets one. Its spending on education has remained at 4.1% of GDP since 2015, but its share of public expenditure has declined 1.5 percentage points to 14.2%.

Among major emerging economies, China too meets one benchmark, at 4% of GDP (11.9% of public spending), while figures for Brazil are 5.6% and 12.9%. South Africa meets both, at 6% and 19.1%, while Indonesia, Bangladesh and Pakistan meet neither.





The pattern is common among developed economies too: the US, UK, Germany and France meet the GDP threshold but not the public expenditure benchmark, while Sweden and Switzerland meet both.

Unesco noted that richer countries tend to meet the GDP benchmark but not the public expenditure threshold because they raise more revenue, while education often accounts for a larger share of budgets in poorer countries.

Latest data show 39 of 205 countries, or 19%, meeting both benchmarks, while 72, or 35%, meet neither.

Another 64 countries, including India, spend above 4% of GDP but below 15% of public expenditure. Among high-income countries, 11% meet both benchmarks and 50% follow India's pattern.

India, however, has larger unmet schooling needs. Lower secondary completion has risen from 81% in 2015 to 86% but remains 13 percentage points below its 99% benchmark. Even Unesco's "feasible" 2025 benchmark of 90% is four points above the latest rate.

This is despite programmes operating at scale. Unesco's India profile says Samagra Shiksha supports about 15.6 crore learners, while PM-Poshan covers around 11.8 crore children in 11.2 lakh government and aided schools. The trend is part of a broader global concern. The scorecard concludes that, on average, countries are "moving away" from the public education expenditure benchmarks of at least 4% of GDP or 15% of total public expenditure.

World.title: Govt. urged to withdraw permission for bars within 100-metre radius of Tasmac liquor outlets
World.content:
The People’s Movement Against Drugs has opposed the decision of the State government to allow bars to be set up within 100-metre radius of Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) liquor outlets, replacing the existing requirement that bars should be attached to the shops.

As per the Government Order, there was no need for bars to be attached to the Tasmac liquor outlets. The bars can be established anywhere within 100-metre radius of the outlets. It is said that the move was aimed at increasing the participation in the tender process and breaking the monopoly of a few operators who had dominated bar contracts for years.

However, the move has drawn opposition from a section of people. The People’s Movement Against Drugs said that the bars had been functioning within the premises of Tasmac liquor outlets. The decision would enable the licence holders to set up bars in thickly populated areas. They might attract more youth who could get addicted to liquor. Such as decision should not have been made when people were against the functioning of Tasmac liquor outlets.

J. Kennedy of the movement said the TVK government, which had captured power with the support of young people and women, should withdraw the decision. Otherwise, the movement would stage protests.

World.title: Jharkhand student protest highlights August 8, 2026: Govt. talks with another faction of protestors end without breakthrough, stir to continue
World.content:
This live blog is closed now

‘Jharkhand govt. assured us of a quick decision to resolve issues raised by students,’ said JPSC JSSC Candidates’ Forum leader after talks with govt. on alleged irregularities over recruitment examinations. ‘Protest to continue until all demands, including cancellation of 14th JPSC exam, are met,’ said the delegation of students.

Also read: Years of delayed exams, bribery allegations provoke Jharkhand protests

Jharkhand Minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu on Saturday (August 8, 2026) announced that the State government has released a dedicated email ID to collect suggestions from students and stakeholders for policy reforms. The students’ protest under the JPSS-JSCC Reform Manch over alleged irregularities in competitive exams entered its 15th day on Saturday (August 8, 2026) after talks between the State government and the student protestors failed to break the deadlock.

World.title: Nearly half of those who figured in electoral rolls of 2024 now under ASDDO
World.content:
A comparison of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) data with the 2024 Lok Sabha election figures suggest an unusual pattern in Bengaluru — the number of electors placed under the Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others (ASDDO) category under the SIR is now almost as large as the number of people who actually turned out to vote just two years ago across three Lok Sabha constituencies that fall under Bengaluru Urban limits.

Unique case of south

The comparison is most significant in the Bengaluru South Lok Sabha constituency. While 53.34% of the electorate voted in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, 50.5% of the present electorate has now been placed under the ASDDO category. This suggests that the constituency now has fewer voters outside the ASDDO category than the number of votes cast in the 2024 election.

In absolute numbers, more than 12.49 lakh votes were cast in 2024, while more than 11.93 lakh electors are now under ASDDO.

Though the comparison does not establish that those now under ASDDO are the same electors who voted in 2024, yet, the numbers throw up a striking anomaly — only 49.5% of the present electorate (11,69,775 electors) remains outside ASDDO, even though over 12.49 lakh votes were cast in the constituency in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. In absolute terms, 79,567 more votes were cast in 2024 than the number of electors presently remaining outside ASDDO.

Voters marked under ASDDO face deletion from the electoral roll unless they establish that they have been wrongly categorised.

Bengaluru Central also presents a similar picture. Around 54.08% of the electorate voted in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, accounting for about 13.16 lakh votes. The latest SIR data shows 46.99% of the present electorate, or around 11.56 lakh electors, under ASDDO. This means around 13.04 lakh voters currently remain outside the ASDDO category, compared with about 13.16 lakh votes cast in the 2024 Lok Sabha election — a difference of only around 12,000.

Bengaluru North shows a similar, though less extreme, pattern. The constituency recorded a voter turnout of 54.5% in the 2024 polls, when around 17.52 lakh votes were cast. Under the ongoing SIR, 45.84% of the present electorate, or around 14.94 lakh electors, have been placed under ASDDO.

This leaves around 17.65 lakh voters outside the ASDDO category, only around 13,000 more than the 17.52 lakh votes cast in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.

Bengaluru South and Central, therefore, present the most considerable anomalies among the three constituencies, with the number of electors remaining outside ASDDO falling below the number of votes actually cast in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. In Bengaluru North, the remaining electorate is still higher than the 2024 vote count, but only by a relatively narrow margin.

Taken together, however, the trend is even more striking. Across Bengaluru South, Central and North, around 42.39 lakh electors now remain outside ASDDO, lower than the 43.18 lakh votes cast across the three constituencies in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.

Suspected duplicate

Officials maintained that the figures are not unusual and attributed the high ASDDO numbers to suspected duplicate voters.

“Most of these voters have voter IDs in other States or districts. But unless they admit that they have another voter ID elsewhere, we cannot classify them as duplicate. So, they are being marked as permanently shifted, which is why the number of shifted voters is high,” a senior official said.

However, the official did not explain how the authorities identify that a person has another voter ID if they are not classifying them as duplicates. Nor did the official explain why, if they possess such information, they are not acting on it.

World.title: Arjun Ayanki arrested in Kannur after days long police search
World.content:
Arjun Ayanki, a key accused in several criminal cases, was arrested by the police in Kannur after more than two days of intensive search. He was reportedly taken into custody on Sunday (August 9, 2026) from an apartment in Kannur city, where he had been staying in hiding.

The arrest was made by a police team led by the Northern Range Deputy Inspector General. Ayanki allegedly attempted to flee when the police reached the apartment and was apprehended at around 2.30 a.m. Another person believed to be his friend was also present at the apartment. He was arrested based on a tip off from an auto driver.

The police had intensified the search after Ayanki allegedly threatened police officers through social media following his release on bail. The Kerala High Court had rejected his anticipatory bail in the case.

Ayanki and his associates had earlier been taken into custody on suspicion of assembling near Kothamangalam for criminal activities. After securing bail, Ayanki allegedly posted threatening and abusive messages targeting the Kothamangalam inspector who led the raid and the Oonnukal Station House Officer through social media platforms.

Despite the rejection of his anticipatory bail plea, Ayanki allegedly continued to remain in hiding while challenging and threatening police officers through social media, prompting the police to intensify efforts to locate him.

After his arrest, he was brought to Kannur District Hospital for medical examination and taken back to Kannur Town station. He is likely to be shifted to Ernakulam after formally registering his arrest in Kannur. Further action is expected to be taken on the direction of the Additional Director General of Police in charge of law and order.

Ayanki, a native of Kappakkadavu in Azhikode, began his political activities as a DYFI unit secretary and later became prominent on social media as a CPI(M) cyber activist. He gained a substantial following by aggressively targeting political opponents online.

His name, however, later became associated with organised criminal activities. He gained notoriety in connection with the Karipur gold smuggling case and was allegedly involved in gangs that intercepted and robbed smuggled gold being transported from airports.

He is also a key accused in the Ramnattukara gold smuggling-related incident in which five people were killed.

Cases relating to an alleged attempt to run over members of a gold smuggling gang with a vehicle, besides cases registered by the Customs Department in connection with gold smuggling, are also pending against him.

Following the emergence of his alleged criminal links, the DYFI expelled Ayanki from the organisation. CPI(M) leadership has repeatedly maintained that the party has no association with cyber or quotation gangs.

World.title: SIR: Deadline for enumeration phase in Karnataka extended again; draft rolls to be published on August 24
World.content:
The enumeration phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which was scheduled to end on Saturday, has been extended till August 17, the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Karnataka, announced on Friday. This is the second extension granted for the exercise.

The draft electoral rolls, scheduled to be published on August 17, will now be released on August 24. The period for filing claims and objections will run from August 24 to September 23, while the final electoral rolls will be published on October 27.

The extension comes days after civil society groups urged the Election Commission to extend the exercise following the publication of the Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others (ASDDO) list, arguing that voters needed adequate time to check whether they had been wrongly classified and approach their Booth Level Officers (BLOs) for corrections.

Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president B.K. Hariprasad had also written to the Karnataka CEO on August 6, seeking a 15-day extension.

With the deadline now extended, voters whose names have been wrongly included in the ASDDO list have time till August 17 to get their details corrected.

As of 4 p.m. on Friday, only 182 enumeration forms were pending digitisation across the State — from Bengaluru South and Belagavi districts.

Meanwhile, the share of voters placed under the ASDDO category has declined from 20.02% on August 5 to 19.81%, indicating that many voters had been wrongly placed under this category.

World.title: Students using BMTC buses on NICE Road must pay toll fee, says corporation
World.content:
Students travelling on the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) buses via NICE Road will have to pay the applicable toll user fee if they opt for the toll road despite alternative routes being available, the transport corporation clarified on Friday, responding to reports on toll charges levied on student pass holders.

In a press release, the BMTC said the user fee is collected only to recover the toll charges it pays for operating buses on NICE Road. The corporation said the amount is not an additional component of the regular passenger fare but is linked specifically to the use of the toll road.

The BMTC said that students are provided free bus passes under the government's student pass scheme and are allowed one or two route changes, wherever necessary, if there is no direct bus service between their residence and educational institution.

The corporation added that students holding concessional passes are allowed to travel free on toll routes where no alternative roads are available, such as routes to Devanahalli, Doddaballapura, Hoskote and Kanakapura.

However, as alternative roads exist for journeys involving the NICE Road, students are expected to use those routes if they wish to avoid paying the toll user fee. Those choosing to travel via the NICE Road despite alternative options must pay the applicable toll charge.

World.title: ATREE unveils LakeRevive tool for science-based lake restoration
World.content:
Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE) on Friday unveiled and disseminated LakeRevive 1.0 tool, a portal that will help contractors, engineers, other professionals and civic activists to make decisions on suitable Nature-based Solutions (NbS) for lake rejuvenation.

The scientific lake restoration requires moving beyond one-size-fits-all interventions and towards context-specific planning, researchers said at the workshop on Friday.

Priyanka Jamwal, senior fellow and convenor of ATREE’s Water and Society Programme, argued for the need to redefine how restoration success is measured.

She argued that restoration goals should be based on context-specific lake health indicators (water, biodiversity and community) rather than uniform water quality standards. This is where the LakeRevive 1.0 tool comes in. The tool is a “decision-support tool that assists people in selecting appropriate nature-based solutions (NbS)”.

Step-by-step solutions

Based on a set of parameters about any given lake, input by the user, the tool recommends step-by-step solutions.

It uses total phosphorus (TP) levels as a restoration benchmark.

It helps users choose what interventions like wetlands, artificial islands etc. suit the lake conditions best.

K. Jaiprakash, retired secretary to the Government of Karnataka, Water Resources Department, said restoring Bengaluru’s lakes had to have an integrated approach that connects lakes, stormwater drains, streams and rivers.

He said, “Scientific planning, technology, government support and community participation must work together to revive urban freshwater ecosystems.”

The workshop on Friday had several stakeholders including government agencies and citizens from communities around lakes, give feedback on the tool as ATREE embarks on creating the LakeRevive 2.0 tool.

World.title: Five arrested for blackmailing, assaulting man in Choolaimedu
World.content:
The Choolaimedu police arrested five people on Saturday (August 8, 2026) for allegedly blackmailing and assaulting a 30-year-old man.

A senior city police official said Sudharsan, a resident of Padmanabha Nagar who works for a pharmaceutical company, had recently married Krishnaveni. He had allegedly contacted a woman named Namitha, who lived near his house, and spoken to her about marrying her.

According to the police, she recorded their conversation and, along with her lawyer friend, Monisha, allegedly demanded ₹5 lakh from Sudharsan to keep the recording secret. The two women allegedly contacted Sudharsan a few days ago and, when he told them that he did not have the money, assaulted him, the police said.

Based on a complaint filed by the Choolaimedu police, a team after conducting an investigation arrested Namitha, 21, Monisha, 26, her husband Balakrishnan, 30, Ganesh, 28, and Sivaranjani, 21.

They were arrested under six sections, including charges of illegal confinement, criminal intimidation, and causing grievous hurt. All five individuals were produced before the Saidapet Court and remanded to judicial custody.

World.title: Initial findings of second post-mortem show multiple injuries on Mir Raza Ali, police surgeon says
World.content:
The initial findings of the second post-mortem examination of 25-year-old business owner Mir Raza Ali revealed multiple injuries and a congealed black substance in his mouth and throat, Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed said on Saturday.

Raza, owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

His body was exhumed earlier today after the Sindh government restored the original medical board.

Dr Summaiya told Dawn that Raza had multiple injuries to his head and face, including fractures to his nasal bone and skull. She said there were also injuries to his right flank and feet.

The police surgeon added that a congealed black substance was found in Raza’s mouth and throat.

Regarding the bullet wound, she said there was a fractured rib in the back, which was the entry point of the gunshot, while the bullet exited through the front.

She further said that DNA samples had been collected and sent to a laboratory, along with samples for chemical analysis and gunshot residue testing.

The cause of death, she added, would remain reserved until the laboratory reports were received.

‘Tortured and murdered’

Advocate Jibran Nasir, representing the family of the 25-year-old, alleged on Saturday evening that Raza had been tortured before being murdered, hours after his second post-mortem was conducted, and demanded that the entire investigation team be replaced.

Speaking to the media in the evening, Nasir said the initial report of the second post-mortem answered “14 questions” and detailed some of the alleged injuries Raza had sustained before his death.

“This was murder following torture — the murder of a happy, ambitious and educated young man from Karachi,” he alleged.

“He had an injury on his chin,” the advocate said, adding that Raza’s eye sockets were compressed and that traces of a foreign substance were found.

“Samples were taken and sent to a lab to see if there are any chemical traces,” he told reporters.

The lawyer also claimed that Raza had wounds to his forehead and a fractured nose, as well as swelling and congealed blood around his lower jaw, consistent with having been punched.

“There is a fracture to his temple above his ear, indicating he was struck,” he alleged.

“In the tongue area, a congealed black substance was discovered, which is not naturally found in the body. This substance has been taken and sent to a lab to see what he was forced to ingest.”

Continuing the description, he also claimed that internal muscles in Raza’s throat were covered in the same black substance, and that a broken hyoid bone and muscle damage suggested that he also was strangled.

“Now we come to the firearm injury, where it was earlier said that he was shot in the chest and the bullet exited through his back,” Nasir said.

“We have now proven 110 per cent that the bullet entered his back and exited after breaking and fracturing his ribs.”

The family’s lawyer also criticised senior police officials, alleging that they “do not want to investigate, but rather humiliate, harass and exhaust the family”.

“They are finding months-old recordings and frustrating, emotionally exhausting and humiliating Mir Hussain and Maryam Hussain. Are you investigating or harassing them? They sat them in their offices and told them repeatedly, ‘It’s a suicide, accept it’. Our city’s AIG was saying this,” the advocate claimed further.

Nasir added that he and the family had “no faith” in the AIG or the SSP’s investigation team and that they wanted the entire team changed, including senior officers.

“If they appoint the same kind of officers, such as those doctors from Jamshoro and Hyderabad, then we will approach the court,” he added.

“But have no doubts about it: senior officers spent 10 days with the parents and misguided them into believing it was a suicide,” Nasir alleged.

Raza’s father, Mir Hussain, told reporters that he had maintained since July 30 that his son’s death was a brutal murder.

“We saw the body and told them [that it was murder], but they kept saying, ‘Suicide, suicide, suicide,’” he said. “Sometimes the SSP would talk to us; the IG would say that the matter had been resolved but there was a problem in the report.

“If your entire police station investigates based on post-mortem reports, then how can someone in such a position of responsibility say something like this?”

Mir Hussain said it “brought us peace” to learn that their claims that Raza had been attacked before his death were true.

“We have said it was murder from the start,” he added. “Why are they hiding the killers?”

Speaking to the media earlier today, Nasir said the investigation officer was present when the body was exhumed and examined, while all eight members of the medical team were also present. The deceased’s parents were nearby and, “most importantly”, a judicial magistrate was present as well.

The lawyer also contended that “incomplete CCTV footage and out-of-context messages” had been used to fuel rumours and draw hasty conclusions since Raza’s death.

While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, investigators probing the incident continue to build their case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

Commenting on the medical board controversy, Nasir expressed concern that the government did not provide any reason for changing the medical board overnight on Friday.

The lawyer said the victim’s family did not need “character certificates” for the doctors on the medical board.

He expressed hope that the medical board’s report would be received by Saturday evening, which would help clarify the circumstances of the young businessman’s death.

The report would clearly indicate if the incident was a murder or suicide, Nasir said, adding that the “police will be under even more pressure” once that question was cleared up.

He reiterated that the report would answer the question of whether it was “self-inflicted or a murder”.

Nasir further said he was surprised to know that the police had shared audio evidence with the media before revealing it to the parents of the victim, who found out about it from TV reports.

Nasir expressed gratitude to the judiciary for intervening in the case, adding that “the work that police could not do in eight to nine days was done in two days after judicial intervention”.

Separately, a PPP delegation comprising MPAs Asif Moosa and Saima Agha visited Raza’s family to convey their condolences.

Moosa assured the bereaved family that Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar and Sindh Inspector General Javed Alam Odho were monitoring the case.

He affirmed that efforts were being made for a transparent inquiry so that justice can be served.

Saima said the probe will be taken forward once the post-mortem report is compiled, asserting that the culprits will be punished. She further said the PPP stood with the victim’s family.

Medical board controversy

The exhumation, which was scheduled for Friday morning, was postponed after the deceased’s family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of the medical board and inclusion of members from outside Karachi division.

On Thursday, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Raza’s father, Mir Hussain Ali, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The court ruling came after a controversy emerged between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding the post-mortem examination.

Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself, said some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. Prof Dr Naseem Ahmed of Dow University of Health Sciences, Dr Farah Waseem of Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Amir Hassan Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, and Dr Mohammed Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon office, were the other members of the board.

However, in the early hours of Friday, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan.

On Friday morning, Raza’s family was present at the Tariq Road graveyard for the exhumation, which was then deferred.

Standing alongside Raza’s father, Nasir had accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts and held the police, health department and the Sindh government responsible for the delay.

World.title: Voting on remaining AJK Poonch division seats may be held by Aug 20-21, says CEC
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal said on Saturday that the Election Commission had decided, for security reasons, to first complete the electoral process in four constituencies of Bagh and Haveli districts and hinted that polls in the remaining seven constituencies of Poonch division could be held by Aug 20 or 21.

Talking to a group of journalists at his office, he said the commission would be in a position to announce the election date for Poonch and Sudhnoti within the next seven days, adding that voters in the two districts would have to be given time to campaign.

Poonch division, comprising 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti districts — has a total of 1,154,626 registered voters.

Monday’s polling, however, will be held in four constituencies in Bagh and Haveli, where 460,371 voters — 238,664 men and 221,707 women — are eligible to cast their ballots at 803 polling stations with 1,254 polling booths.

A total of 82 candidates are in the fray, with the highest number of 30 contesting LA-14 (Central Bagh) and the lowest, nine, in LA-17 (Haveli). The contestants include one sitting prime minister, two former prime ministers, one sitting minister, three former ministers and one sitting member of the AJK Council.

“I appeal to the people of Bagh and Haveli to complete the process of change through their votes,” Justice Mughal said, adding that voting was “not only their democratic right but also a religious obligation, as it is their responsibility to ensure that the trust reaches its rightful recipient”.

He said security personnel had already reached Bagh and Haveli, while transportation of polling material was under way under the supervision of the army.

Asked about the oath-taking of successful candidates, the chief election commissioner said there was no constitutional impediment to them taking the oath.

“However, there are moral grounds for withholding the oath until the House becomes complete following the completion of the electoral process in Poonch and Sudhnoti districts.”

“Once the House is complete, elections will be held for the reserved seats, followed by elections for the speaker, deputy speaker and leader of the House,” he added.

Justice Mughal said eight security personnel would be deployed at each polling station identified as highly sensitive from a security perspective.

“The security personnel who had been deployed in Muzaffarabad have now been moved to Bagh and Haveli,” he said.

He added that the Election Commission would try to have internet services restored in Bagh and Haveli on Aug 9 and 10 to facilitate the compilation and transmission of election results.

On allegations of rigging levelled by political leaders, the CEC said the Election Commission had limitations in responding to such claims.

“The Election Commission has its own limitations. Political leaders’ allegations cannot be answered through statements or political rhetoric,” he said.

“Once the elections are completed, we will bring the facts before the public — whether rigging took place and, if so, who was responsible for it,” he added.

Explaining the procedure for compiling results, Justice Mughal said: “The Returning Officer compiles the result, while counting is conducted beforehand in the presence of the polling agents of the candidates.”

Earlier today, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said that the PML-N would form the government in AJK with a two-thirds majority.

World.title: JI announces Aug 16 sit-ins in provincial capitals to protest petroleum levy
World.content:
LAHORE: Jamaat-i-Islami Pakistan (JI) has decided to intensify its campaign against the petroleum levy and inflation, announcing simultaneous sit-ins in all four provincial capitals on August 16 to press the government to withdraw the levy.

The decision was taken after extensive deliberations at a special meeting of JI’s central and provincial office-bearers, chaired by party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman at Mansoora on Saturday.

Rehman said the sit-ins would be staged outside the Punjab chief minister’s house in Lahore and the governor houses in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh and Balochistan.

Under the plan, the JI and its youth and women’s wings will participate in Independence Day activities on August 14, using the occasion to mobilise people around the party’s vision of a just system.

The JI chief added that the previous day’s nationwide protest had given the party’s campaign against the petroleum levy and inflation a new direction and fresh momentum; and that over 510 organised and peaceful protests were held across the country, with people from across Pakistan participating.

He said the protests had demonstrated that the JI was “becoming a symbol of national unity”, as people from Chitral, Malakand, Hazara and central Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, among others, had raised their voices against the petroleum levy.

The JI chief added that the public had rejected the levy and wanted petrol prices reduced to Rs225 per litre. Rehman accused the ruling elite of pushing ordinary citizens into an unbearable inflationary crisis while refusing to cut their own privileges and expenditures.

The party chief also claimed the rulers were “unwilling to give up official aircraft, reduce government vehicle expenses or end perks such as free fuel and electricity”, while students, motorcyclists, workers and farmers were being burdened with indirect taxes on petroleum products.

“Even people whose incomes were below the taxable threshold were effectively being taxed through fuel prices,” he added.

Rehman said the JI had previously taken to the streets to force the government to negotiate with independent power producers (IPP), after initially refusing to engage with them.

He added that negotiations had been held with 17 to 18 IPPs, resulting in some reduction in electricity prices, but the process was subsequently halted.

“The unresolved energy crisis and rising prices have fuelled an inflationary storm that is affecting every segment of society, particularly salaried people, the middle class and poor families,” Rehman said.

He warned that the public could no longer be left to suffer the consequences of government policies and said the rulers would have to deliver their rights.

Rehman also welcomed the recently signed defence agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, describing it as “a positive development for the Muslim world”.

He said closer cooperation among Islamic countries could lead to a strong bloc and reduce Pakistan’s and the wider Muslim world’s dependence on external powers.

Additionally, he proposed expanding the defence cooperation to include Iran, Qatar, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Indonesia, saying efforts should gradually be made to bring all Muslim countries into such a framework.

“Muslim countries should overcome their differences, strengthen mutual cooperation and build collective capacity to face regional and global challenges,” Rehman emphasised.

A day prior, several major thoroughfares in Karachi were blocked or affected by traffic disruptions as the JI held sit-ins as part of the nationwide demonstration against the petroleum levy.

Responding to the protest, Sindh government spokesperson Sadia Javed said the petroleum levy was a federal matter and questioned why Karachi’s citizens were being “punished” through road closures.

“Jamaat-i-Islami is using the protest to score political points instead of serving the public,” she alleged, adding that the party should focus on the performance of its local government representatives to improve conditions for Karachi’s residents.

World.title: Pakistan, New Zealand seek to boost cooperation in agri, education sectors
World.content:
Pakistan and New Zealand discussed boosting cooperation in various fields, with a special focus on agriculture and education, as the two sides held a Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meeting in Wellington, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday.

The third Pakistan-New Zealand JTC meeting and the fifth round of Pakistan-New Zealand Political Consultations were held in Wellington on Thursday, “marking a significant step in deepening bilateral engagement between the two countries”, the FO said.

A key outcome of the meetings was the signing of the Education Cooperation Arrangement between Pakistan and New Zealand, which is “expected to significantly deepen collaboration in the education sector”.

At the JTC meeting, both sides “deliberated on improving market access and enhancing cooperation in sustainable agriculture, including exploring technical collaboration in wool production and plant protection”, the FO said.

The discussions focused on bolstering bilateral trade and investment, with particular emphasis on technology, education and services.

Institutional mechanisms to further economic cooperation were also discussed, the statement added.

Commerce Secretary Jawad Paul Khawaja represented Pakistan during the JTC meeting, while Grahame Morton, deputy secretary of the Americas and Asia Group at New Zealand’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, headed the other delegation.

Meanwhile, during the political consultations, both sides conducted a comprehensive review of bilateral relations. They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, and agreed to enhance coordination within multilateral forums.

Additional Foreign Secretary (Asia Pacific) Ambassador Dr Syed Ali Asad Gillani co-chaired the Pakistani side at the political consultations, while Morton headed the New Zealand delegation.

Islamabad and Wellington “explored avenues to strengthen cooperation across a wide spectrum of areas of mutual interest, including high-level exchanges, economic development, science and technology, education, counterterrorism, transnational crime, and people-to-people ties”, the FO said.

Ambassador Gillani briefed the New Zealand side on Pakistan’s efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East, as Islamabad remains actively engaged in efforts to defuse the Strait of Hormuz stand-off.

Morton “acknowledged Pakistan’s constructive role in the Middle East peace process”, the FO statement said.

Gillani also discussed the situation in South Asia, including in India-occupied Kashmir (IoK) and India’s “continued violations” of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT).

India had unilaterally decided to put the IWT in abeyance in late April 2025 after hostilities flared up between the two neighbours last year. The issue of water has remained a bitter point of contention between the nuclear-armed nations since then, with Islamabad repeatedly raising the issue on international platforms.

The overall discussions between Pakistan and New Zealand “provided an opportunity to assess progress in bilateral ties, identify new areas for partnership, and reaffirm the shared commitment to a forward-looking and mutually beneficial relationship”, the FO noted.

Pakistan and New Zealand enjoy cordial and friendly relations, with both countries being members of the Commonwealth.

Bilateral trade stands at $12 million, with Pakistan’s major exports being textile products, apparel, rice, leather articles and sports goods, according to the FO’s website.

Main imports from New Zealand include dairy products, wood pulp, paper, edible oil, wood, iron steel and electrical machinery.

Agriculture and education were also among areas of cooperation discussed between the two sides when former military dictator Gen Pervez Musharraf visited Auckland in June 2005.

Last month, India and New Zealand signed a free trade deal as they sought to boost exports amid global economic uncertainty made worse by the war in the Middle East.

World.title: Rana Sanaullah says PML-N will form govt in AJK with two-thirds majority
World.content:
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Saturday that the PML-N would form the government in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) with a two-thirds majority.

He made the remarks while addressing a rally in Bagh ahead of the third phase of elections in the region. The third phase was originally slated to be held in the 11 constituencies of Poonch division, but will now only be held in its Bagh and Haveli districts due to law and order concerns.

Addressing the rally, Sanaullah said that in the first two phases, the PML-N had secured 24 seats. He said that six more seats were required for a two-thirds majority government.

Expressing confidence that the public will vote for his PML-N, the minister asserted that four more seats would be added following the August 10 polls, while five more would be added when polls would be held in the rest of Poonch Division.
